b9e186be749410dd: PRAGUE: Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres scored in the first half to hand Arsenal a 2-1 win at Slavia Prague in the Champions League on Wednesday.
Arsenal got back to winning ways in Europe after a 2-2 draw at Bayern last month, reaching 10 points from four Champions League games so far, while Slavia have a single point in the standings.
"We have to value the fact that it's very difficult to win away from home. We've done it against a really tough opponent, as we expected," said Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta.
"Two very different halves. The first one where we played at a really high level in terms of tempo, intensity, quality and clarity in what we had to do," he added.
The Premier League champions were quick to take control of the game in chilly conditions in the Czech capital.
Madueke reaped the rewards on nine minutes.
Gyokeres controlled David Raya's long clearance with his chest and passed the ball instinctively to Madueke sprinting behind him down the right flank.
Madueke left the Slavia back four behind him with ease and beat diving Ukrainian teenager Nazar Domchak in the Slavia goal with a low shot.
Gyokeres, one of six changes in Mikel Arteta's starting line-up from Sunday's 1-0 win at Liverpool, made it 2-0 on 38 minutes.
He beat Domchak with a neat shot off the far post after a one-two with Mikel Merino on the edge of the Slavia box.
- 'Far from our standards' -
Czech champions Slavia were sluggish throughout the first half, producing a single chance when skipper Tomas Holes fired wide from inside the box.
But they stepped up their pace considerably in the second half to stave off a repeat of a 3-0 home loss to the Gunners in the competition exactly a year ago.
Slavia's Polish midfielder Oskar Kubiak forced a diving save from Raya seconds into the second half.
Gabriel Magalhaes and Raya cleared two headers off the goalline in quick succession with 15 minutes to go, while David Zima fired over the bar.
Raya then forced a Kubiak header onto the post.
Slavia scored a consolation goal in the 90th minute when David Jurasek's cross bounced through the Arsenal defence and Wiktor Nowak blasted the ball into the net from close range.
"(We) scored two goals. It should have been three, four or five. We didn't make that gap," said Arteta.
"Right from the beginning, we were extremely far from our standards and everything that we have to do... in everything that we discussed to avoid the game that we played in the second half."
It was the 23rd straight game without a win for the hosts in the Champions League, taking them within one of equalling AEK Athens' all-time record from 1992-2006. - AFP

9004bd879b06afb8: KUALA LUMPUR: Motorists will enjoy a 50 per cent toll discount for two days in conjunction with Deepavali, with the government allocating RM20.11 million in compensation to participating highway concessionaires.
Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said the discount would take effect from midnight this Friday until 11.59pm on Saturday.
The initiative covers Class 1 private vehicles at all toll plazas, as well as Class 2 vehicles at the Penang Bridge.

However, the discount will not apply at border toll plazas, namely the Sultan Iskandar Building (BSI) toll plaza on the North-South Expressway and Tanjung Kupang toll plaza on the Malaysia-Singapore Second Link.
In a statement today, Nanta said the initiative reflected the government's continued commitment to safeguarding the people's welfare and well-being.
He said the discount was expected to ease travel costs, particularly for Hindus returning to their hometowns or visiting family members to celebrate Deepavali.
Motorists are advised to plan their journeys early to avoid traffic congestion.
They should also ensure their Touch 'n Go cards or eWallets have sufficient balance, observe speed limits, maintain a safe distance from other vehicles and take adequate rest to avoid driver fatigue.
Motorists are also encouraged to check the latest traffic updates and highway incidents through the Malaysian Highway Authority's official channels to better plan their journeys.
7eb4292703fc6b55: KUALA LUMPUR: Aviation-related stocks surged in early trade on Thursday as a sharp decline in crude oil prices raised hopes of lower fuel costs for airlines.
AirAsia Group Bhd and Capital A Bhd emerged as Bursa Malaysia's two most actively traded counters, with both recording double-digit gains.
As at 9.30am, AirAsia Group's shares had climbed as much as 20.88 per cent, or 9.5 sen, to 55 sen from Wednesday's close of 45.5 sen.
The stock subsequently eased to 52 sen, still up 14.29 per cent, or 6.5 sen, with more than 26 million shares changing hands.
At that price, the airline's market capitalisation stood at RM1.74 billion.
Meanwhile, its associate Capital A rose as much as 15.22 per cent, or 3.5 sen, to 26.5 sen from Wednesday's close of 23 sen.
At the time of writing, Capital A was trading at 25.5 sen, up 10.87 per cent, or 2.5 sen, with more than 21 million shares traded.
The counter's market capitalisation stood at RM1.14 billion.
The gains came as global oil prices plunged on Wednesday amid growing expectations of a possible end to the US-Israeli war with Iran following the US midterm elections.
Brent crude futures for January delivery fell US$8.98, or 8.7 per cent, to settle at US$94.62 a barrel on the ICE Futures Europe exchange.
Lower oil prices could ease fuel costs for airlines, potentially improving their operating margins.
ba30e5c61910be68: LEIPZIG: Erling Haaland's 78th-minute strike helped Manchester City shake off a mini-slump with a 3-2 Champions League win at RB Leipzig on Wednesday.
After an excellent start to the season, City had lost two Premier League games in a row either side of beating Brighton on penalties in the League Cup.
The visitors twice went ahead – through a Castello Lukeba own goal and an Enzo Fernandez header – only to be pegged back by goals from Ridle Baku and Antonio Nusa.
Despite having scored more against Leipzig than any other opponents in his career, Haaland had few chances but was right on the spot to turn in an Elliot Anderson cross for the winner.
"For me I think it's easy. It's around 100 minutes a game to just stay fully focused," Haaland told reporters.
"In this period it was about trying to wait for the right moment and attack it in the right way and put it in the back of the net and that's exactly what I did."
Haaland has now scored 13 times in nine matches against Leipzig, including a memorable five-goal performance in a 7-0 rout in March 2023.
Despite the victory, City were well below their usual best against a Leipzig side in a rebuilding process under new coach Martin Demichelis.
City coach Enzo Maresca, who arrived in the summer, conceded his side were still a "work in progress" but praised Haaland.
"It's important that he's on his game. We know that at any moment he can help us, he can score goals," Maresca said.
Maresca backed under-fire goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma, who was out of position for Baku's equaliser.
"It's not a concern... We are talking about a mistake. A few minutes before he made a save that no keeper in the world could make."

Nusa's performance was a highlight for the hosts, with Haaland's Norway teammate now on six goals and seven assists in 14 matches this season as Leipzig look to replace Yan Diomande, who left for Real Madrid in the summer.
"It's a pity, to be honest," Nusa told TNT Sports. "I feel like we deserved more today and you end up with zero points. It's not a good feeling."
- City's mini-slide -
City travelled to Germany having lost two Premier League games in a row for the first time since August 2025.
Leipzig had won just one from three in the Champions League before Wednesday but had been excellent at home, winning five from five while scoring 19 goals without conceding once.
Haaland was handed the captain's armband for the first time this season but it was another Norwegian, Leipzig's Nusa, who impressed early.
Nusa forced Donnarumma to tip a shot over the crossbar with 14 minutes gone.
Leipzig looked more comfortable but then conceded in embarrassing fashion with 37 minutes gone when Lukeba bungled a Nico O'Reilly cut-back into his own goal.

Christoph Baumgartner forced an excellent save from Donnarumma just after the break but Leipzig were soon level when Baku threaded a low shot in from an acute angle with the Italian out of position off his line.
Haaland's first dangerous moment came shortly after Baku's equaliser, when he forced a close-range save from Maarten Vandevoordt.
Fernandez had City back in front just before the hour mark when he headed in a lovely Iliman Ndiaye cross, but Leipzig restored parity just three minutes later.
Christopher Nkunku linked up with Nusa just four minutes after coming off the bench, allowing the Norwegian to cut a low shot across the face of goal and in.
When Anderson broke down the right flank with 12 minutes left, Haaland immediately adjusted his run towards the far post, where he waited to tap in the England midfielder's pinpoint cross. - AFP

166e2907db2bbb8d: JOHOR BARU: The annual Deepavali bazaar in Johor Baru's Little India has drawn local shoppers and visitors from Singapore seeking traditional snacks, clothing and other festive goods.
Its strategic location in the city centre, close to the Johor Causeway, makes it a popular destination for Singaporeans seeking a variety of items ahead of the festival.
The annual bazaar offers a wide selection of goods, including traditional snacks, clothing, home decorations and women's accessories.
Singaporean visitor T. Murthy, 78, said he and his family travelled to the city every year to buy traditional snacks sold at the bazaar.
"There is a wide variety of snacks here, including muruku, which taste very good because they are traditionally homemade.
"They are also much cheaper and more affordable than those sold in Singapore. That is why I enjoy shopping here for Deepavali," he said when met yesterday.
The bazaar also reflects the spirit of unity, with visitors from different communities taking the opportunity to shop and experience the festive preparations.
Clothing trader S. Candrika, 39, said her stall selling Punjabi attire attracted not only members of the local Indian community but also shoppers from other ethnic groups.
"We have regular customers who return to shop here every year. We also receive visits from Malay and Chinese customers who buy traditional Punjabi clothes.
"Some buy them to wear when visiting their Indian friends, while others purchase them for events with an Indian traditional theme," she said.
Another trader, J. Sathis, 31, said unpredictable weather and occasional rain in recent weeks had affected businesses to some extent.
"This area is well known and is one of the attractions for visitors during the Deepavali festive season.
"I expect the number of visitors to continue increasing as the festival approaches on Sunday," he said.S

b10528f867a9e9bb: PETALING JAYA, Nov 5 — The Transport Ministry is actively working to resolve train service congestion and overcome technical challenges faced by rail operators, says Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook.
“Rapid KL is working to address various technical challenges. We will resolve these technical issues to improve the service,” he said.
Loke told reporters this at his ministry’s get-together event with Tamil media practitioners at the Tropicana Golf and Country Resort here yesterday.
On Oct 30, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim directed the Transport Minister to swiftly resolve train congestion issues, expressing concern that they disrupt the public’s daily routine.
The directive followed a complaint posted by a user on the Threads platform to Anwar regarding overcrowding at train stations.
Meanwhile, Loke said train frequencies have been increased for the festive season to encourage more people to use public transport when returning to their hometowns.
He said Electric Train Service (ETS) trips from Kuala Lumpur to west coast states, including Kedah and Johor, received an encouraging response, with additional services scheduled ahead of Deepavali.
“We have added trips ahead of Deepavali, and Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) is working to ensure service frequency is increased so that more people can take the train home,” he said.
Earlier, speaking on the event, Loke said it served as a platform to strengthen ties between the ministry and Tamil media practitioners in conjunction with Deepavali.
He noted that the media plays a vital role in disseminating information on ministry policies and services to all segments of society, including the Indian community.

Loke added that close cooperation with media practitioners is essential to ensure clear communication on road safety, public transport, the Road Transport Department (JPJ), and the aviation sector. — Bernama

e10d8f02bb372b5c: NEW YORK: A Citigroup employee was killed in a shooting at the bank's office in Tampa, Florida on Wednesday, Chief Executive Jane Fraser said, while authorities said the suspect involved was also dead.
In a memo to staff, Fraser said the bank was still learning the details of what happened and was working closely with local law enforcement.
"The Tampa campus is secure, and we are adding additional security to all of our other sites as necessary," Fraser said.
Hilsboro County Sheriff Chad Chronister said in a statement earlier on Wednesday that "the suspect involved in the Citibank Active Threat scene is deceased."
The sheriff also said 365 deputies had responded and that he believed it was a targeted incident.
17a6de2932699041: LYON: French club Lyon confirmed on Wednesday the departure of Portuguese coach Paulo Fonseca to Sporting Lisbon with a compensation fee of five million euros ($5.6 million) paid to the Ligue 1 side.
Fonseca, 53, joined Lyon in January 2025 as a replacement for Pierre Sage and was contracted until the end of this season.

"Paulo came to see me last week to say he had received an offer from Sporting and had accepted it, explaining it was a choice of the heart as it is his boyhood club," Lyon sporting director Matthieu Louis-Jean told AFP.

"I wasn't expecting this at all. I tried to understand his reasons, but it quickly became clear that, for him, it was an offer he couldn't refuse and for us, it would be difficult, because you can't keep someone against their will."

The former Porto, Shakhtar Donetsk, Lille and AC Milan coach guided Lyon to a fourth-place finish last term, but they missed out on this season's Champions League league phase after losing in the play-offs.

"I believe this is the right moment for me to be the coach of Sporting... This club has always been special to me," Fonseca told reporters after signing a deal with Sporting keeping him at the club until 2030.

Fonseca's spell at Lyon came during a turbulent financial period. In June 2025, French football's financial watchdog provisionally relegated the club to Ligue 2 before the decision was overturned on appeal, subject to a strict programme of cost-cutting measures and player sales.
The club also stuck by Fonseca after he was given a nine-month domestic ban last year for an angry altercation with a referee.
While thanking Fonseca for his commitment, Lyon expressed "deep regret" regarding what they described as an "unexpected decision" mid-season with the club third in Ligue 1.
Lyon are expected to appoint a permanent successor during the upcoming international break, with former Braga coach Carlos Vicens reportedly among the leading candidates.
Assistant Jorge Maciel will take charge of Lyon on an interim basis for the club's next two matches, Thursday's Europa League fixture against Real Sociedad and Sunday's Ligue 1 trip to Brest. - AFP
56ed3b4d41bbf2da: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is scheduled to attend five programmes in Melaka tomorrow, including participating in Pakatan Harapan (PH) campaign activities in conjunction with the Melaka State Election.
Anwar said two of the programmes he would be attending are the 2026 Prime Minister’s Golden Hand Award (MATEPM) ceremony and the Melaka State Madani Aspirations Tour.

“Insya-Allah, I will be in Melaka tomorrow for several engagements in this historic state. I will first visit Universiti Teknikal Malaysia Melaka (UTeM) to meet educators and students at an official event, before heading to several other locations to boost the Harapan momentum in Melaka,” he said in a Facebook post yesterday.

Based on the schedule shared in the post, Anwar is slated to begin his visit by attending the MATEPM 2026 at Dewan Canselor, UTeM, at 2.30 pm, before joining the Melaka State Madani Aspirations Tour for the Klebang state constituency in Taman Bukit Rambai at 4.45 pm.

In the evening, the PH chairman is scheduled to attend the ‘Malam Harapan’ programme at Dewan Pay Fong, SJK Pay Fong, at 7.30 pm, followed by the ‘Malam Ramah Mesra Melaka Rumah Kita Bersama PMX’ programme for the Paya Rumput constituency at Taman Seri Karanjong, Paya Rumput, at 8.30 pm.

Polling is on Nov 14, with early voting set for Nov 10. — Bernama
7a36e70b102acc0e: TUMPAT: Food and essential supplies distributed ahead of the northeast monsoon have brought relief to more than 3,000 residents in 12 villages.
Some villagers, meanwhile, have begun buying and stockpiling dry food to prepare for the monsoon season rather than relying solely on aid.
Teluk Renjuna villager Mohd Faiza Ibrahim, 46, said most residents tended to stay home during the monsoon as persistent rain and rising river levels made it difficult to travel.
"Conditions become more difficult when strong winds raise fears of falling trees, as our village is along the Kelantan River delta, which is lined with coconut trees.
"Boats are the main mode of transport for residents. If the roads remain safe, we can still travel by motorcycle. However, when floodwaters reach the village, residents have to stay at home.
"We are grateful that assistance is provided every year," he said.
Faiza was speaking during a distribution of supplies by the Social Welfare Department at the forward base in Kampung Teluk Renjuna yesterday.

The aid, comprising rice, cooking oil, sardines, sugar and tea, was transported in six boats along a 10km stretch of the Kelantan River, from the Padang Kemahkotaan jetty to the Kampung Teluk Renjuna jetty.
Grocery shop owner Mohd Husin Mohammad, 54, said he had also increased stocks at his premises ahead of the monsoon.
He said petrol was among the essential supplies needed by residents, as boats were their main mode of transport, and he had to ensure his shop maintained an adequate fuel supply.

"Even during the monsoon season and rainy weather, I have to ensure my shop has sufficient supplies. If I need to replenish stocks, I have no problem navigating my boat to the mainland to make purchases, as I am used to it.
"My other preparation is to move goods in the shop to higher ground, as floodwaters overflow onto the land and enter the premises whenever flooding occurs," he said.
Tumpat, in northern Kelantan, is home to numerous small river islands along the Kelantan River delta, where communities are vulnerable to flooding during the annual northeast monsoon.
659a3b0c85012646: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia opened higher on Thursday, tracking Wall Street's positive overnight performance as improving global sentiment and easing geopolitical concerns lifted investor confidence.
At 9.10 am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 11.16 points, or 0.69 per cent, to 1,627.72 from Wednesday's close of 1,616.56.
The benchmark index opened 6.72 points higher at 1,623.28.
In the broader market, losers outnumbered gainers 241 to 232, while 268 counters were unchanged, 2,020 untraded and 10 suspended.
Turnover stood at 263.87 million units worth RM148.93 million.

Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said the local bourse could see renewed buying interest following the previous session's profit-taking activities, supported by lower crude oil prices and improving external sentiment.

He said Wall Street had closed sharply higher following the Democrats' significant gains in the US midterm elections, which helped ease some of the economic and geopolitical uncertainties weighing on markets.
"Back home, we believe the index may see strong buying support today, particularly as crude oil prices have retreated," he told Bernama.

Thong noted that Brent crude had weakened to below US$95 per barrel amid hopes of easing tensions in West Asia, providing support to market sentiment, with the FBM KLCI expected to trend within the 1,615 to 1,630 range today.
Among the 30 FBM KLCI constituents, 24 counters were trading higher, one lower and five unchanged.

Banking heavyweight stocks were all firmer ahead of Bank Negara Malaysia's Overnight Policy Rate decision, due later in the afternoon, with expectations of an interest rate hike lending support to the local currency.

Of the heavyweight stocks, Maybank and IHH Healthcare were 10 sen firmer at RM10.00 and RM7.88, respectively, while Public Bank rose four sen to RM4.81, CIMB gained 11 sen to RM7.02, and Tenaga Nasional was flat at RM13.14.

In active trade, AirAsia rose eight sen to 53.5 sen, Capital A gained three sen to 26 sen, while Dagang Nexchange, VS Industry and MMAG were half a sen lower at 41.5 sen, 33 sen and two sen, respectively.

Nestle led the top gainers, rising RM1.00 to RM94.50, while Hong Leong Bank gained 26 sen to RM21.50, Allianz rose 20 sen to RM19.72, Hong Leong Financial gained 18 sen to RM17.64, and PPB advanced 14 sen to RM9.00.

Among the top losers, MPI fell RM1.20 to RM39.42, Vitrox lost 36 sen to RM10.54, Hengyuan Refining dropped 32 sen to RM3.30, UWC slipped 19 sen to RM7.01, and Petronas Chemicals fell 18 sen to RM4.52.
On the index board, the FBM Emas Index surged 52.26 points to 12,130.24, while the FBM Top 100 Index gained 57.67 points to 11,942.75.
The FBM Mid 70 Index fell 17.14 points to 17,494.11, the FBM Emas Shariah Index advanced 13.78 points to 12,118.21, and the FBM ACE Index declined 15.85 points to 5,404.93.

Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index edged down 0.60 of a point to 177.61, while the Energy Index fell 13.91 points to 814.01. The Financial Services Index gained 200.40 points to 18,786.71, while the Plantation Index rose 45.79 points to 8,807.67.

505f6456dd500bf0: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Highway concessionaire AFA Prime Berhad has activated its Travel Time Advisory for the Kuala Lumpur-Karak Highway (KLK) and the East Coast Expressway Phase 1 (LPT1) ahead of an anticipated holiday traffic surge for Deepavali.

The staggered travel schedule aims to ease bottlenecks across the arterial eastern corridor, particularly at the high-volume Gombak, Bentong, and Jabor toll plazas that link the Klang Valley to Pahang, Terengganu, and Kelantan.
Under its “Smart Travel” roadmap, the operator has segmented recommended departure windows by state destination to distribute traffic evenly across peak holiday dates.
For outbound journeys from Kuala Lumpur and Selangor on Saturday, Nov 7, motorists passing through the Gombak Toll Plaza are advised to stagger their departures according to their destination.
Travellers heading to Kelantan are advised to start earliest, between 6am and 9am or from 5pm to 8pm.

Motorists bound for Terengganu should depart between 9am and 12pm or from 8pm to 11pm, while those heading to Pahang are urged to enter the expressway between 12pm and 4pm or during the secondary 8pm to 11pm window.
For the return commute towards the Klang Valley on Monday, Nov 9, drivers originating from Pahang are encouraged to use any toll plaza between 7am and 10am or from 7pm to 11pm.
Motorists returning from Terengganu through the Jabor Toll Plaza should target travel between 10am and 1pm or from 8pm to 10pm.
Meanwhile, traffic heading back from Kelantan via the Bentong Toll Plaza is advised to move between 4pm and 8pm or during the late 9pm to midnight slot.
To maximise efficiency, motorists are also encouraged to take advantage of “Free Travel Hours” during the midnight to 6am off-peak window on both designated dates.
Private car owners are specifically cautioned to avoid heavy express bus departure surges at the Gombak Toll Plaza, which peak between 9.30am and 12 noon as well as between 9.30pm and midnight.

AFA Prime managing director and chief executive officer Ahmad Faizi Latifi Ahmad Faiz reminded motorists to navigate cautiously through ongoing construction zones along the KLK, where active widening works are currently underway as part of the RM2.1 billion KLK Expansion project.

“We urge all road users to comply with the traffic instructions and signage at work zones, to reduce speed and to drive with extra care,” he said, adding that dedicated emergency response teams and patrol units will be deployed at strategic points along both expressways to provide rapid assistance.
5207dc50ab1653ff: ATHENS: Federico Valverde lashed home a stunning effort from distance to snatch Real Madrid a late 3-2 victory at AEK Athens on Wednesday in the Champions League and preserve their 100 percent start.

Jose Mourinho's side twice came from behind against the Greek champions before Valverde claimed all three points for his side, level with holders Paris Saint-Germain on four wins from four league phase games.
Aboubakary Koita sent AEK ahead after 12 minutes and Jude Bellingham equalised with a sublime flick for the record 15-time winners.
Stavros Pilios sent the Greek champions ahead with 15 minutes to go but Kylian Mbappe swiftly pulled Madrid level once again, setting the stage for Valverde's late winner.
"Fede has that capability... (but) I didn't ask him to shoot," Mourinho told Movistar about his match-winner, who came on in the second half.

"I told him was that the game was wide open, it was being played at great speed... a fresh player like Fede, with his ability to cover a lot of ground, I told him to attack the space and arrive in the dangerous areas."
Madrid have now won seven straight games across all competitions.
"We fought for (the victory), and with the score at 2-2 we didn't settle," added Mourinho.
"It would always be an acceptable result, we'd be on 10 points, but we wanted more."
Mourinho started with Vinicius Junior on the left flank, after he missed the team's previous two matches through suspension, in La Liga.
The hosts started with huge energy at the Agia Sophia stadium and it was not overly surprising when they took an early lead.
Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois saved well from former Los Blancos striker Luka Jovic before Koita sent AEK ahead.
The Mauritanian winger shifted cleverly inside Marc Cucurella and thumped home at the near post, catching out Courtois.
The Belgian goalkeeper saved again from Jovic as AEK tried to make their strong start count.
However they inevitably began to tire and Madrid began to take the reins in the Greek capital.
Kylian Mbappe fired over and Bellingham netted from close range but was shown to be offside. Moments later the England international scored again and nobody could deny him this one.
Cucurella fired in a low cross and Bellingham produced a brilliant flicked finish to beat goalkeeper Alberto Brignoli.
Former Chelsea defender Cucurella tested Brignoli and Bernardo Silva nodded off-target before the interval as Mourinho's team controlled the game.
Brignoli pushed away Eder Militao's long-range effort early in the second half and Lazaros Rota blocked superbly to deny the heavily-involved Cucurella.
- Another fightback -
Mbappe bent a shot narrowly wide of the top corner with Italian stopper Brignoli at full stretch.
The France forward was frustrated by the AEK defence when Vinicius turned sharply and found him with a high pass, but the striker's shot was blocked.
AEK reclaimed the lead in the 75th minute when the impressive Koita gently nudged the ball into Pilios's path and the Albania international finished through Courtois's legs from close range.
Madrid immediately responded with Bellingham playing Denzel Dumfries in down the right. The Netherlands defender rolled a low ball across the six-yard box and this time Mbappe was able to finish.
It was Mbappe's fourth goal in four Champions League games this season, netting once in each, and his 16th across all competitions.
Madrid substitute Endrick sent Mbappe through on goal with five minutes remaining but Brignoli produced a sensational save to tip his strike against the crossbar.
Valverde refused to give up on the three points and in the 92nd minute he lashed home across Brignoli to keep Madrid perfect.
Koita, who had been substituted, was sent off after the game for apparent dissent.
Valverde thanked his team-mates for backing him when he gets the chance to shoot.

"Sometimes I overthink it, and well, as I always say, I'm grateful to the players, to my teammates, because they're the ones who give me the confidence so that, in those moments, I can make that decision and have the courage to hit it," he said. - AFP

82d3c2f4fcd0b24c: SYDNEY: Australia's 188-year-old department store chain, David Jones, was placed into voluntary administration on Thursday, as rising costs, sluggish retail sales and supply chain pressures weighed on its business.
David Jones stores will continue to operate under the control of FTI Consulting, the appointed receivers, while the firm reviews current operations.
McGrathNicol has been appointed as voluntary administrators.

"A transaction process seeking offers for a recapitalisation of the business or a sale as a going concern will commence immediately, and will be managed by McGrathNicol," FTI Consulting and McGrathNicol said in a joint statement.
"We will manage this process carefully, mindful of the impact on some stakeholders but also recognising the need for difficult decisions."
Founded in Sydney in 1838 by Welsh immigrant David Jones, the upscale retailer describes itself as the world's oldest continuously operating department store.
With about 6,000 employees across 38 stores in Australia and New Zealand, David Jones is one of Australia's most recognisable brands and predates London's Harrods by more than a decade.
For generations, Australian shoppers have turned to David Jones for clothing and accessories for milestone occasions, from formal wear to school and graduation attire.

However, like overseas counterparts, the retailer has struggled for more than a decade as the rise of online shopping and competition from fast-fashion chains have steadily eroded its traditional department store business model.

Its latest owner was private equity firm Anchorage Capital Partners, which bought it from South African retailer Woolworths in 2022 for a price media reported at the time was about A$100 million (US$70.09 million).
David Jones CEO Erica Berchtold said the retailer had "a well-developed plan on how to reset the business for the future".
She added that the company would work with the administrators, receivers and its secured lender during the voluntary administration process, Australia's closest equivalent to Chapter 11 bankruptcy.

Luxury US department store owner Saks Global, which battled similar retail trends, emerged from Chapter 11 in June after nearly five months with fewer than half of its previous stores and a quarter of its debt.

Scentre Group, which owns and operates Westfield shopping centres in Australia and New Zealand, offered a lifeline to David Jones, but it was rejected by Anchorage Capital, ABC News reported, citing Scentre CEO Elliott Rusanow.
David Jones has stores at 17 Westfield locations.
In a statement to the Australian Securities Exchange on Wednesday, Scentre said David Jones had paid rent up to September 30.

ef8441fb27923b2b: ISTANBUL: Dirk Kuyt got the better of his former club Liverpool as Fenerbahce twice came from behind for a famous 3-2 win in Istanbul on Wednesday that breathed new life into their Champions League campaign.

Trey Nyoni and substitute Alexander Isak twice put the visitors in front.
But Liverpool, who lost twice away to Galatasaray last season, were beaten again in Istanbul as Englishmen Mason Greenwood and Archie Brown levelled before Vedat Muriqi's winner.
"We've gone twice in front after having good moments, controlling the game, we've found the goals but after we've conceded in situations we should definitely defend better," said Iraola.
Fenerbahce's interim boss Kuyt, who spent six years at Anfield as a player, was taking charge for just the second time after Ismail Kartal quit last week.
The Turkish giants had taken just two points from their opening three Champions League games but made the most of Liverpool's generosity at the back.

Nyoni retained his place and capped another fine performance with his first Liverpool goal from the edge of the box after Fenerbahce failed to clear Dominik Szoboszlai's cross.
The home side bounced back just four minutes later when Alisson Becker was deceived by Greenwood's deflected free-kick to equalise.
Iraola unleashed Isak, Wirtz and Cody Gakpo from the bench just after the hour mark in search of a winner and got an almost immediate reward.
Isak was afforded far too much space to head in Gakpo's cross.
But again Liverpool quickly handed back their advantage.
Gakpo's touch inadvertently deflected a cross beyond Alisson to give Brown an easy tap-in at the back post.
Liverpool then conceded for the 10th time in four Champions League games when Muriqi outmuscled Jeremy Jacquet to a looping cross and steered a header into the bottom corner.

"I think we've put ourselves in good positions, so that today if we lose this game it's not a chaos situation," said Isak. "We just need to get back to winning ways and if we win the next game, we are back to a really good position."
Victory moves Fenerbahce move up to 19th in the 36-team table.
Only the top eight qualify directly for the last 16 with ninth to 24th facing off in a two-legged play-off. - AFP

b307ab9ce0727765: KUALA LUMPUR: Will Bank Negara Malaysia raise interest rates today? And if it does, how much more could you end up paying on your housing loan?
The central bank will announce its final interest rate decision of the year at 3pm, with most economists expecting it to keep the overnight policy rate (OPR) unchanged at 2.75 per cent.
However, some believe stronger economic growth has strengthened the case for raising the OPR to three per cent, effectively reversing the pre-emptive cut made in July 2025.
Bank Negara lowered the OPR by 25 basis points last year to cushion the economy against global uncertainties, particularly US trade tariffs.
But Malaysia's economy has since performed better than expected, expanding 5.3 per cent in the third quarter of 2026, according to advance estimates.
Some economists believe this gives Bank Negara room to "normalise" interest rates by returning the OPR to its previous level.
What would a rate hike mean for your loans?
For homeowners with floating-rate mortgages, a 25-basis-point increase would generally mean higher monthly repayments.
For example, a RM300,000 outstanding housing loan with 25 years remaining and an effective interest rate of four per cent would carry monthly repayments of about RM1,584.
If the rate increases to 4.25 per cent, repayments could rise to approximately RM1,625, or RM41 more a month.
For a RM500,000 loan under the same conditions, the increase would be around RM68 a month.
These are illustrative calculations. Actual repayments depend on individual loan terms and banks' adjustments.
What about car loans and savings?
Existing fixed-rate car loans generally would not be affected, although variable-rate financing could become more expensive.
Credit card interest rates also do not automatically increase when the OPR rises.
Savers, meanwhile, could benefit from better fixed deposit returns if banks adjust their deposit rates upwards.
Will Bank Negara actually raise rates?
The majority of economists expect the central bank to hold off for now, particularly with inflation remaining manageable at 1.8 per cent in September.
Others argue that stronger growth warrants a return to three per cent to prevent borrowing costs from remaining unnecessarily low.
The debate comes as several central banks, including those in the UK and Japan, have raised interest rates this year amid renewed inflation pressures.
For Malaysia, however, the question is whether stronger growth alone is sufficient reason to reverse last year's precautionary cut.
Bank Negara's decision at 3pm could provide an important indication of where borrowing costs are headed in 2027.

9377170f8571f0e6: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump's stunning midterm defeat by the Democrats has upended another US election — the race to replace him in the White House in 2028.
The crushing defeat for the Republicans is particularly stinging for Vice-President JD Vance, who had been the frontrunner but now risks being seen as tied to his lame-duck boss.
But the midterms are a potential launchpad for rising Democratic stars such as Georgia Senator Jon Ossoff, whose youthful appeal has already drawn comparisons with former president Barack Obama.
Republicans in turmoil
The MAGA coalition that propelled Trump to power in 2016 and 2024 effectively collapsed in Tuesday's midterms, leaving any presumptive Republican heir with a mountain to climb.

Long seen as the odds-on favourite for the Republican nomination in 2028, Vance is the most obvious victim after hitching his wagon to Trump throughout the midterm campaign, attending rallies in swing states.
The ambitious 42-year-old quickly tried to distance himself from the electoral disaster, blaming it on Trump's unpopular war on Iran in a lengthy post on X on Wednesday.
But voters are likely to reject his attempts to disown Trump.

It is a familiar problem for US vice-presidents. Former Democratic candidate and vice-president Kamala Harris faced a similar problem in 2024 when she said that "there's not a thing that comes to mind" when asked how she would differentiate herself from Joe Biden.
"The bad news for Vance is that sitting vice-presidents seldom win the presidency," James Lindsay of the Council on Foreign Relations said.
Trump's Secretary of State Marco Rubio's name has also been bandied about.
Rubio, 55, has kept a far lower profile during the midterms, but any top official in Trump's administration will struggle to wash their hands of the Iran war.
The Republicans' midterm disaster could, however, boost other possible candidates.
Florida Governor Ron DeSantis, 48, who ran against Trump for the Republican nomination in 2024, has suddenly become very vocal.
He described the Democratic sweep as "the political equivalent of a meteor strike" and pointed out that it was only in his own state that Republicans held them off.

Texas Senator Ted Cruz, 55, has also left the door open, having run against Trump in 2016 — although his chances may have been harmed by the Democrats' stunning Senate and gubernatorial victories in his state in the midterms.
Democrats on a high
The Democratic field is crowded, but the midterms have given some likely candidates a boost.
Ossoff's re-election as a Georgia senator has fuelled speculation about a 2028 run by the telegenic politician, who has already gained attention for mocking Trump's relationship with a young staffer.
The 39-year-old has said that he has "zero interest in running for president", but his swiftly declared victory in Georgia — and his victory speech — have bolstered his standing in the party.
Before the midterms, Kamala Harris, 62, had been the favourite for the nomination, but many in the party would prefer someone without a losing track record.
Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro, 53, who was interviewed by Harris to be her running mate in 2024, had a good night on Tuesday as he stormed to re-election in the key battleground state.

Outgoing California Governor Gavin Newsom, 59, is another big name who has repeatedly taken on Trump. In an interview with AFP in September, he predicted that Trump's presidency "as we know it would be over after the midterms".
But Newsom, like Harris, may be seen as more of an old-guard figure in a party that is looking to its rising stars.

A prominent but potentially divisive choice would be left-wing New York Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, who said in September that she was weighing a run, musing about whether a Latina could win in a country that rejected female nominees in 2016 and 2024.

Other possible contenders include former Chicago mayor Rahm Emanuel, JB Pritzker, the billionaire Illinois governor who set out a lengthy national agenda after winning a third term on Tuesday, Kentucky Governor Andy Beshear, and Arizona Senator and former astronaut Mark Kelly.

c05c49afb7ef3a03: PARIS: The cooling system of France's blood bank has been hit by a cyberattack similar to the hacker attack targeting refrigeration systems across Europe earlier this week, the EFS bank said on Wednesday, reported German Press Agency (dpa).

be1e875ccbf2b87e: LEIPZIG, Nov 5 — Erling Haaland’s 78th-minute strike helped Manchester City shake off a mini-slump with a 3-2 Champions League win at RB Leipzig yesterday.
After an excellent start to the season, City had lost two Premier League games in a row either side of beating Brighton on penalties in the League Cup.
The visitors twice went ahead—through a Castello Lukeba own goal and an Enzo Fernandez header—only to be pegged back by goals from Ridle Baku and Antonio Nusa.
Despite having scored more against Leipzig than any other opponents in his career, Haaland had few chances but was right on the spot to turn in an Elliot Anderson cross for the winner.
“For me I think it’s easy. It’s around 100 minutes a game to just stay fully focused,” Haaland told reporters.
“In this period it was about trying to wait for the right moment and attack it in the right way and put it in the back of the net and that’s exactly what I did.”
Haaland has now scored 13 times in nine matches against Leipzig, including a memorable five-goal performance in a 7-0 rout in March 2023.
Despite the victory, City were well below their usual best against a Leipzig side in a rebuilding process under new coach Martin Demichelis.
City coach Enzo Maresca, who arrived in the summer, conceded his side were still a “work in progress” but praised Haaland.
“It’s important that he’s on his game. We know that at any moment he can help us, he can score goals,” Maresca said.
Maresca backed under-fire goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma, who was out of position for Baku’s equaliser.
“It’s not a concern... We are talking about a mistake. A few minutes before he made a save that no keeper in the world could make.”

Nusa’s performance was a highlight for the hosts, with Haaland’s Norway teammate now on six goals and seven assists in 14 matches this season as Leipzig look to replace Yan Diomande, who left for Real Madrid in the summer.
“It’s a pity, to be honest,” Nusa told TNT Sports. “I feel like we deserved more today and you end up with zero points. It’s not a good feeling.”
City’s mini-slide
City travelled to Germany having lost two Premier League games in a row for the first time since August 2025.
Leipzig had won just one from three in the Champions League before Wednesday but had been excellent at home, winning five from five while scoring 19 goals without conceding once.
Haaland was handed the captain’s armband for the first time this season but it was another Norwegian, Leipzig’s Nusa, who impressed early.
Nusa forced Donnarumma to tip a shot over the crossbar with 14 minutes gone.
Leipzig looked more comfortable but then conceded in embarrassing fashion with 37 minutes gone when Lukeba bungled a Nico O’Reilly cut-back into his own goal.

Christoph Baumgartner forced an excellent save from Donnarumma just after the break but Leipzig were soon level when Baku threaded a low shot in from an acute angle with the Italian out of position off his line.
Haaland’s first dangerous moment came shortly after Baku’s equaliser, when he forced a close-range save from Maarten Vandevoordt.
Fernandez had City back in front just before the hour mark when he headed in a lovely Iliman Ndiaye cross, but Leipzig restored parity just three minutes later.
Christopher Nkunku linked up with Nusa just four minutes after coming off the bench, allowing the Norwegian to cut a low shot across the face of goal and in.
When Anderson broke down the right flank with 12 minutes left, Haaland immediately adjusted his run towards the far post, where he waited to tap in the England midfielder’s pinpoint cross. — AFP

The question follows a public disagreement over spending at the Rural and Regional Development Ministry, which is led by Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.

115f8a5c72186dfb: HOUSTON/NEW YORK: Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has rattled the state's data centre industry with a campaign pledge to halt new projects, injecting new uncertainty into one of the country's fastest-growing markets for server warehouses worth billions of dollars.

With plentiful energy supplies, relatively cheap land and a pro-business policy, Texas has become one of the leading regions in the world for data center developments. Big Tech companies including Meta, Google and Microsoft have announced major data center projects in the state over the past two years.

The data center industry there had already come under pressure before the midterms. On August 3, Greg Abbott became one of the first Republican governors in the US to halt the connection of new data centers to the state's electric grid amid growing opposition from rural communities and a surge in requests to connect to the state's power grid.
Abbott, who had supported data centers a month earlier, also ordered a comprehensive audit of the projects, with a focus on power demand, environmental impacts and tax breaks given to developers.

Even before Hinojosa's dramatic upset of Abbott on Tuesday, she had vowed to take the crackdown on data centers a step further by banning all data center approvals until the state legislature passes laws "to protect Texans, so that Texans have a seat at the table to decide if and how data centers come into our community."

By the time Texas halted data centers connecting to its grid, state grid operator ERCOT said it was tracking more than 400 gigawatts of data center projects – roughly equivalent to what it would take to power the entire US South – seeking to connect to the grid.

Abbott's about-face also threw tens of billions of dollars of data center projects planned in Texas into jeopardy and raised doubts over whether hundreds of millions in grid deposits paid by data centers seeking to connect to the grid would be returned. Since ordering the audit, Abbott has also taken actions to penalize data center water violations retroactively and temporarily banned the state from issuing air permits for the projects.

Abbott, however, did not issue a formal moratorium on data centers, which Hinojosa has vowed to do. Certain measures by Abbott also had a near-term expiration date, like the air permit ban and the audit, which was expected to conclude at the end of 2026.

The new governor's administration and the Texas legislature will now need to get up to speed on the state's patchwork of recent actions and regulations on data centers before solidifying a new set of laws and rules around the industry, said Austin McCarty, a Texas data center attorney with K&L Gates.
"It's a brand-new day in Texas for a ton of what was probably considered settled policy – not just for data centers, but energy as a whole," McCarty said.

Some Texas data center projects are likely to get delayed or to see developers exit the state entirely, while others are expected to speed up the process of completing and powering up the centers before new restrictions take hold, he added.

The Data Center Coalition, which represents Big Tech and other data center developers, said its members would continue to pursue their infrastructure build-out in the state while working with state and local governments.

"Enhancing affordability, creating jobs, and keeping the state's economy strong are top priorities for Texans. Data centers can continue to play a crucial role in advancing those priorities by bringing investment to local communities," said Jess Heck, Texas director of government affairs at the Data Center Coalition.
SWEEPING OPPOSITION

Some 42 per cent of registered voters in a Reuters/Ipsos poll published this week said limiting the construction of data centers used to power AI was very important or the most important issue for them.

"The data centers connect economic development to everyday concerns," University of Houston political scientist Brandon Rottinghaus said a day before the vote, citing electricity bills, water supplies and property rights.
Polling showed rural voters, who are "at the epicenter of so many of these fights," were unhappy with the spread of data centers heading into the election, he said.

Brittany Kaiser, CEO of data center developer Alpha Compute, said the results in Texas and Ohio, where winning candidates made opposition to data centers a big part of their platforms, will make some companies question whether to invest in those states. Developers that don't already have signed contracts and financing are more likely to look elsewhere, including abroad in Canada, Mexico and Europe, she said.

"What I really think is that a lot of companies are going to be investing in very red states and purple states," Kaiser said in an interview on Wednesday. "Definitely over the past six months, that's been most of the pipeline that I've created for my own business, because it looks like less of a political risk."

Kaiser said the skepticism comes from voters' fears about AI and what data centers mean for their electricity bills, the environment and jobs, and that many AI CEOs have "not made it easy to be excited about the future of AI."

Industry efforts to keep data center costs from being passed on to ratepayers never reached voters, she said, and developers now need to engage directly with legislators, regulators and communities and go beyond regulatory compliance to be good neighbors.
"I definitely never thought data centers would be in a position where people would rather live near a nuclear facility or a prison," Kaiser said.

Some 76 per cent of voters nationwide said they opposed the construction of a new data center in their community, according to an NBC and SSRS exit poll. Ahead of the vote, a University of Houston poll in October found that 79 per cent of likely Texas voters supported limits on the number of data centers that can be built in the state.

Texas accounts for 25 per cent of planned data center capacity in the US, according to a note by Goldman Sachs. New Democratic governors in the Lone Star State and other burgeoning data center hubs, including Georgia and Michigan, could result in state legislation that would end tax breaks for the industry, tighten environmental and electricity rules and pave the way for towns and cities to pass their own moratoria, the note said.

"Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now," Elon Musk, who supported Abbott in the election and had spent US$158 million to promote Texas Republican US Senate candidate Ken Paxton alone, wrote early Wednesday on X.

However, at 10am, an acquaintance contacted the mother to inform her that the child had been found unconscious in the pond, located about 50m from their home.
Firefighters retrieved the boy from the water.
Tan said investigations showed the victim was believed to have gone to the pond alone to fish, following the discovery of a fishing rod near the scene.
A medical officer pronounced the child dead at 11.15am. A post-mortem examination confirmed the cause of death as drowning.
Tan said the case has been classified as a sudden death report, with further investigations ongoing.

d21991623813df94: MELAKA: Sales of traditional Melaka dodol have doubled for a local producer, driven by an influx of political party campaign teams and visitors from outside the state during the 16th Melaka election campaign.

"Most people who come to Melaka to campaign, whether from within or outside the state, will look for local favourites such as asam pedas and dodol.
"Dodol is among the traditional delicacies they seek out and buy to take home or give to their families," she said when met here today.
Nur Aliyah said visits by political party campaign teams usually increased towards the end of the campaign period, based on her family's experience in previous elections.
Some campaign teams also placed bulk orders to distribute dodol to villagers or serve it during community programmes, she added.
She said the family business was established in 1960 by her great-grandmother, the late Tijah Maakti, and had been passed down through four generations.
After Tijah's death, the business was continued by Nur Aliyah's grandmother, the late Echa Ngah, for about 15 years before her father took over when her grandmother became unwell.
Nur Aliyah said the family continued to use traditional wood-fired cooking methods, which gave the dodol its distinctive aroma and texture compared with machine-made products.
"We sell dodol in several packaging options, including jars containing 36 pieces for RM40, 500g packs for RM13 and smaller packs containing 12 pieces for RM13.
"We operate daily from 9am to 9pm and also receive visits from school students who want to see how this traditional delicacy is made," she said.

f17a491c466e321c: PETALING JAYA: Attacking Malay institutions to discredit Umno and Barisan Nasional (BN) will do little to help Pakatan Harapan (PH) win votes in the Melaka election, according to an analyst.
Neither will personal attacks on rival candidates, another political pundit says.

“PH can campaign as loudly and aggressively in Melaka as it did in previous state elections, so long as it exercises caution when it comes to Malay institutions,” Azmi Hassan of Akademi Nusantara told FMT.
He pointed out that PH’s aggressive attacks on Umno over the Tabung Haji (TH) fiasco during the Negeri Sembilan campaign had failed to resonate with voters.
“I think the Malay voters rejected PH in part due to its aggressive approach and their attempt to link Umno with the failures of TH, Felda and UiTM Holdings,” he said.

Azmi said the prevailing perception among the Malays was that the DAP had tried to “destroy” TH when the government established the special purpose vehicle Urusharta Jamaah Sdn Bhd in 2018 to facilitate the acquisition of TH’s underperforming assets.
That was during Lim Guan Eng’s tenure as finance minister. Lim was also the DAP secretary-general at that time.

A royal commission of inquiry report released in August revealed that poor governance, political interference and financial misrepresentation led TH to report a RM3.4 billion profit despite an RM11 billion deficit from 2014 to 2020.

In Felda, the government revealed that financial mismanagement, aggressive corporate acquisitions and political interference led to a RM10 billion loss in 2017 while UiTM recorded pretax losses amounting to RM157 million over a four-year period from 2017.
“I think you need to be loud and aggressive (in the Melaka campaign), but not by attacking (Umno-BN) directly using the Malay institutions. It does not work,” Azmi said.
He said Melaka PH should focus on showing voters how it can govern the state better than BN, which won the previous state election in 2021.

He was commenting on PH secretary-general Saifuddin Nasution Ismail’s recent statement that the coalition would run a peaceful campaign for the Melaka polls, having learnt that victory does not go to the loudest, but to the most trusted.

Saifuddin’s remarks come as PH enters its fourth state election campaign since the end of last year — following polls in Sabah, Johor and Negeri Sembilan — with little electoral success to show for its efforts.
They won only one of five seats they contested in the Sabah state election in November last year, down from eight seats garnered in the 2020 polls.

In the Johor polls in July, they won eight seats, down from 12 in the previous election in 2022, and in the Negeri Sembilan election in August, they came home with only 11 seats, compared with 17 in the 2023 election.
Refrain from mudslinging
Academic Lau Zhe Wei of International Islamic University of Malaysia said PH campaigners must refrain from personal attacks on individual candidates in the rival camp.
This is especially pertinent when it comes to incumbents who have performed well, such as BN’s Noor Helmy Abdul Halem, who is hoping to win a second term as Duyong assemblyman, he told FMT.

“Helmy is popular among Duyong’s residents, including non-Malays. If you relentlessly criticise your opponents, there will be a backlash,” he said, adding that PH should attack the party and not the candidate.
PH is contesting 24 out of 28 seats in the Nov 14 state election. It has formed a pact with Bersatu, which is vying for seven seats, clashing with PH in three.
1c5f8252381c9e95: Menurut ahli falsafah dan sejarawan Perancis yang terkenal, Pierre Nora; terdapat satu hubungan erat antara sejarah dan memori. Akan tetapi Nora menegaskan, dalam banyak keadaan memori adalah lebih utama dan dalam banyak keadaan mengatasi sejarah. Ini kerana memori adalah pencarian kebenaran yang objektif a search for objective truth atau satu himpunan bagaimana ia pernah terjadi, a recollection of how it really was.

Sedangkan sejarah tidak sebebas memori, dan kadangkala perlu dikendala. Ini kerana sejarah selalunya mempunyai aspek ideologi dan boleh dimanipulasi, ideological and manipulative. Idea dan gagasan Nora mengenai pertentangan memori melawan sejarah ini boleh ditemukan dalam banyak karya-karya beliau, antara lain The Present. Nation. Memory; Between Memory and History. Problems of Memory Places; World Celebration of Memory; History as Protection from Politics; dan dalam kerja beliau yang paling masyhur, Places of Memory.

Mengapakah Nora lebih berpihak kepada memori berbanding sejarah, sedang beliau adalah seorang sejarawan? Menurut Nora, beliau pertamanya ingin meluruskan semula sejarah dengan membersihkannya dari fakta tertentu.

Fakta-fakta sejarah ini pada Nora telah dimanipulasi oleh agenda politik dan hanya memori secara kolektif yang dapat membetulkan keadaan ini. Nora dalam kerja-kerja akademiknya menyorot bagaimana gerakan politik, pengukuhan identiti kebangsaan Perancis, dan agenda kelompok tertentu boleh mencemarkan sejarah. Tugas sejarawan sebenarnya adalah memelihara atau melindungi memori ini.

Atas alasan inilah Nora melancarkan gagasan beliau yang dikenali sebagai Places of Memory. Bagaimanapun cabaran untuk meluruskan sejarah dengan mencari memori yang benar ini bukanlah mudah, memandangkan memori itu sendiri terputus, tambahan pula tradisi sendiri akan hancur atau ditinggalkan, dan inovasi mengambil tempat sehingga memori kolektif itu sendiri ikut terjejas. Nora menyatakan, memori yang benar hanya datang dari ruang-tempat memori berjejak memory places atau mnemonic places, yang hadir membentuk ruang memori.

Nora menafsirkan konsep places of memory (lieu de memoire) ini sebagai satu fenomena yang signifikan, terzahir ketara atau tidak ketara, yang mana kerana kenekadan masyarakat atau pengaruh zaman telah membentuk sebagai satu lambang warisan untuk bangsa;

Memori kolektif terbentuk oleh kerana memori berjejak ini yang termanifestasi secara benda, fungsi dan lambang. Memori berjejak dalam bentuk benda misalnya adalah monumen, tugu, memorial, perkabungan, penyanjungan, wajah pada stem atau duit kertas, acara yang bersempenakan memori ini, nama jalan; dan lain-lain. Memori yang terputus memerlukan memori berjejak ini supaya dapat diingat kembali dan sekaligus dimurnikan semula sejarahnya. Sesuatu hanya ‘menjadi sejarah setelah memori berakhir, selagi memori dipugar secara kolektif maka sesuatu itu belum menjadi sejarah meskipun sudah berlaku pada masa lampau’; dalam erti kata lain ‘sejarah akan terus hidup jika terus dikenang’.

Harus diingat, memori berjejak Nora selalu dikelirukan oleh ramai sebagai satu tempat, ini kerana terjemahan suntuk place of memory itu dikait dengan physical place, padahal ia telah kehilangan tempat dan lebih kepada simbol atau tanda, kesan, atau jejak.

Saya selalu mengangankan, atau mencita-citakan agar nama Wan Azizah Wan Ismail terlekat dalam memori Malaysia, di saat beliau masih bernafas dan masih hidup. Beliau memiliki tempat dalam memori negara. Saya khuatir meletakkannya dalam sejarah. Ini kerana seperti mana dilihat oleh Nora, sejarah boleh mengalami pemesongan. Buku sejarah boleh diubah oleh pihak yang menang. Sejarah boleh dipadam. Tetapi memori misalnya tidak boleh dipadam. Yazid bin Muawiyah sebagai contoh cuba memadam sejarah mengenai cucu Rasulullah. Dia gagal. Ini kerana Zaynab al Kubra, puteri Fatimah dan Saidina Ali menghidupkan memori abangnya itu dengan segar dan harum. Ia menjadikan kesyahidan itu sentiasa hidup.

Sejarah telah membuktikan bahawa wanita di alam Melayu bukanlah kelompok yang pasif atau hanya berdiri di belakang kejayaan seseorang pimpinan masyarakat. Antara fakta dari lipatan sejarah alam Melayu, dapat dikenali sosok seorang Permaisuri bernama Pramodawardhana yang bertanggungjawab di belakang Kerajaan Majapahit dan Pembangunan Borobudur yang inklusif. Dari era kesultanan hingga ke zaman perjuangan kemerdekaan dan era pemodenan dan digital masa kini, wanita Melayu telah memainkan peranan yang amat signifikan sebagai pemimpin, diplomat, pendidik, usahawan, pemikir sosiobudaya, dan tiang seri utama dalam keharmonian nusa bangsa.

Di saat berlakunya krisis dalam masyarakat, wanita terbukti menjadi penyelamat. Seperti dilakukan oleh Tengku Ampuan Intan Tengku Alang Hussain yang menjadi Yang Dipertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan antara tahun 1869-1872 iaitu ketika berlakunya pertelingkahan untuk merebut kuasa. Watak sedemikian muncul lagi di zaman kita, dengan nama Wan Azizah Wan Ismail.

Selaku timbalan perdana menteri (2018-2020) dan pemimpin di Kementerian Pembangunan Wanita, Keluarga dan Masyarakat (KPWKM), Wan Azizah ketika itu telah melancarkan Pelan Tindakan Kebangsaan Menangani Punca Perkahwinan Bawah Umur (2020-2025). Pelan ini merangkumi strategi menyeluruh berasaskan lima punca utama yang digariskan menerusi kajian mendalam, iaitu kemiskinan sosioekonomi, kekurangan akses kepada pendidikan, kepincangan maklumat kesihatan reproduktif, kelonggaran undang-undang, serta persepsi dan stigma masyarakat. Saya membayangkan bagaimana kiranya memori Wan Azizah ini disuburkan terus. Dan memori itu diberi nyawa apabila lima punca di atas terus dikaji dan diberi solusi oleh sebuah universiti. Kita ahli akademik mengkaji dan memberi solusi, atas nama Wan Azizah. Berbahagi pahala.

Satu lagi tonggak utama dalam perjuangan pemerkasaan wanita yang sentiasa Wan Azizah tekankan ialah pengiktirafan terhadap golongan suri rumah yang memerlukan perlindungan keselamatan sosial yang sewajarnya. Di tangan beliau lahir program i-Suri dan i-Sayang yang hari ini mesti diteruskan sebagai usaha menangani jurang perlindungan sosial. Kerajaan ketika itu melancarkan Skim i-Suri di bawah Caruman Sukarela Insentif Suri bagi memastikan suri rumah berdaftar dalam sistem eKasih mendapat tabungan hari tua di Kumpulan Wang Simpanan Pekerja (KWSP) dengan bantuan insentif kerajaan.

Memori atau legasi kerja bekas timbalan perdana menteri ini mesti dibaja. Ia mesti diberi, bak kata Pierre Nora, sebuah tanah pamah, sebuah watan dan tekad yang dapat menampang places of memory (lieu de memoire) tersebut. Kalau ada rezeki harapnya memori Wan Azizah ini akan dapat ditegakkan di kala beliau masih hidup, dan di kala saya masih berkhidmat sebagai ahli akademik.
Ini hanyalah angan-angan saya. Agar nama Wan Azizah itu abadi, dan mengatasi sejarah. Ia boleh dan Insya-Allah menjadi memori, satu kenangan yang wangi dan lama. Biarkan ia abadi.
Artikel ini adalah pandangan penulis dan tidak semestinya mewakili FMT.
5751d93e5c6bdfe9: PETALING JAYA. Nov 5 — Malaysia should make technology choice for investors an explicit part of its 5G policy, with safeguards that preserve genuine alternatives when network owners or suppliers change, says an analyst.

Samirul Ariff Othman of Global Asia Consulting said having two operators did not automatically guarantee different supplier ecosystems or prevent both networks from becoming dependent on the same critical suppliers.
“Malaysia should make meaningful supplier diversity and the ability to change suppliers' explicit objectives of its 5G policy,” said Samirul.
His comments follow Machang MP Wan Ahmad Fayhsal Wan Ahmad Kamal’s call on Oct 22 for Malaysia to retain Western and Chinese technology options.
Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) uses Ericsson equipment, while U Mobile appointed Huawei and ZTE for its second network.

Samirul said Ministerial Direction No. 7 of 2025 directed the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) to support the dual-network model, including spectrum arrangements and service continuity, but did not itself require a permanent East-West supplier split.
MCMC’s licensing guidelines describe licences as technology- and service-neutral, although individual licences may carry special conditions.

Samirul said he had not identified an explicit, binding requirement in public material guaranteeing distinct supplier ecosystems through future changes, but this did not establish that no safeguard existed.
Operator-specific licence conditions, spectrum conditions or undertakings needed confirmation from MCMC, he said.
“The government should identify the applicable instrument, the obligation it creates and how compliance is enforced,” he said.
He warned that dependence on the same critical suppliers could expose both networks to common software vulnerabilities, supply disruptions or restrictions on technical support.
Samirul proposed a published policy backed by licence or spectrum conditions, procurement requirements and continuing oversight, with obligations applying to both operators and approved successors.

Major ownership, supplier or network-sharing changes that substantially increased common dependence should undergo resilience assessments, while routine purchasing remained a management responsibility, he said.

He said procurement should address security, compatibility, long-term support and credible arrangements for switching suppliers, while implementation must respect existing contracts and allow reasonable transition periods.
“Supplier nationality alone cannot establish whether a network is secure or sufficiently independent,” he said.
He also proposed periodic reporting and fair access to both networks for eligible wholesale customers.
Farlina Said of the Institute of Strategic and International Studies (ISIS) Malaysia said reliable access and service continuity should take priority.
“Diversification is helpful to reduce risks of single points of failure,” she said.

While not recommending a specific regulatory mechanism, Farlina said commercial technology choices might need to account for differing cybersecurity requirements across industries and supply-chain partners for Malaysia to attract international businesses.

Samirul acknowledged that no policy could prevent every future government from changing direction, but published obligations, consultation and parliamentary scrutiny would make continuity more dependable and changes more accountable.

fb96676d3287c87c: MANILA: Philippine inflation accelerated to its fastest pace in almost four years in October as the prolonged Middle East conflict drove up the cost of fuel, electricity and transport in a nation heavily reliant on the region for its energy supplies.

Consumer prices hit 7.8% last month from a year earlier, the highest since an 8.6% print in February 2023, the Philippine Statistics Authority said Thursday. Inflation was 7.2% in September, and the median estimate in a Bloomberg News survey put October’s number at 7.6%.

The acceleration was mainly driven by a jump in transport costs, the authority said. Another factor was a “faster annual increase observed in the housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels index.”

The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas is in the midst of a tightening cycle that included a surprise 50 basis-point rate hike in October to rein in spiraling costs. The central bank had previously said it expected inflation in October to come in between 7.1% to 8.1%.
The Philippine economy is coming under pressure on multiple fronts after posting the second-weakest growth among Southeast Asia’s major economies in the second quarter.

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr’s administration is contending with surging oil prices and a peso at record lows as the Middle East conflict drives up energy costs, while consumer spending is losing steam, business confidence is weakening and El Niño is straining the economy - all with just 18 months to go before the 2028 election.
148d00e0e6e8a33a: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Carlsberg Malaysia has clarified that it was never a sponsor of Hyrox Kuala Lumpur 2026 and holds no commercial involvement in the upcoming fitness competition, further defusing a controversy over marketing graphics that had drawn permit threats from the Youth and Sports Ministry.

In a statement posted to Instagram yesterday, the brewer explained that a newly unveiled regional partnership between Hyrox and Carlsberg in Asia applies exclusively to events staged in Singapore, Hong Kong, Taiwan, and Vietnam, leaving Malaysia deliberately omitted from the arrangement.

“At Carlsberg Malaysia, we adhere to the country’s local laws, regulations, and respect cultural sensitivities,” the company said, reiterating its standard responsible consumption disclaimer that its products are strictly intended for non-Muslims aged 21 and above alongside the hashtag #CelebrateResponsibly.
The multi-day indoor fitness race is slated to take place from Dec 10 to 13 at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre (MITEC) in Kuala Lumpur.

The clarification came ahead of an ultimatum issued by the Youth and Sports Ministry on Wednesday, which warned that it would withhold operating approvals for the event until organisers completely purged the brewer’s branding, logos, and promotional assets from both physical venues and digital promotional channels.
The ministry noted that the organiser’s licence application remained pending and that Putrajaya had disbursed neither state funding nor regulatory clearance for the race.

Authorities cited Article 5.2 of the Safe Sport Code (3rd Edition, 2024), which explicitly prohibits tobacco, vape, and alcohol enterprises from sponsoring, advertising, or showcasing corporate trademarks across sporting events sanctioned by the ministry and its statutory agencies. Youth and Sports Minister Mohammed Taufiq Johari maintained that the government would brook no compromise in ensuring a healthy and safe sporting environment.

The ministry also cautioned organisers that proceeding with an unsanctioned competition violates Section 36(1) of the Sports Development Act 1997, which bars any entity from running sports activities without a formal licence from the Commissioner of Sports Malaysia, an offence punishable by fines up to RM500,000, a maximum five-year jail term, or both.
Hyrox Malaysia subsequently issued an apology across its social media channels, acknowledging that circulating the regional sponsorship graphic had caused distress and offense among the public.

Admitting that the management should have been more mindful of the religious beliefs and cultural norms of Malaysians, the organiser stated: “We got this wrong,” confirming that the decision to exclude Carlsberg from the Kuala Lumpur stop was made in mutual agreement with the brewer while reassuring registered participants that preparations for the race remain on track.
3151b4d3f24cbf3f: TOKYO: The dollar edged lower on Thursday in the aftermath of an overwhelming victory by Democrats in US midterm elections that cleared a major source of uncertainty and fuelled a rally in global equities.

The yen firmed after minutes of the Bank of Japan's September meeting reinforced expectations for further interest rate hikes, while sterling held near a seven-week high ahead of a Bank of England policy decision expected to deliver another rate increase.

Democrats swept to sizable majorities in the Senate and House of Representatives, easing concerns about contested results and spurring gains in US Treasuries and equities around the world. The election result raises prospects of political gridlock in Washington and lowers expectations that US President Donald Trump will resume military strikes against Iran, said Ray Attrill, head of FX strategy at National Australia Bank.

"A lot of the market moves that we're seeing, particularly in bonds, I think can be traced directly to that, as well as a weaker dollar on the back of lower Treasury yields," Attrill said on a podcast.
The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, fell 0.06% to 101.41, after a 0.36% decline in the prior session. The euro was up 0.12% at US$1.1241.
The yen strengthened 0.08% to 158.25 per dollar.

Despite the political shift in the US, expectations for the Federal Reserve's interest rate path remained largely intact. Markets are pricing in an 81.2% chance for a rate increase of at least 25 basis points from the Fed at its December meeting, according to CME FedWatch, up from 77.4% in the prior session.

The ADP National Employment Report showed US private payrolls rose by 86,000 jobs in October, above the 69,000 estimate of economists polled by Reuters. The report was the latest in a string of labour market data this week, which will wind up on Friday with the release of the government's payrolls report.

Sterling was up 0.38% at US$1.3462, after rising to a more than seven-week high of US$1.3503 ahead of the Bank of England's policy announcement on Thursday. The pound was poised for its sixth straight daily gain, its longest run higher since an eight-session streak that ended on July 6.
The BOE expected to raise rates to contend with inflation pressure from soaring energy costs, although it may push back against investors' bets that several more increases will follow next year.

The Bank of Japan meeting minutes from September, when policymakers raised rates to a 31-year high of 1.25%, underscored expectations for further tightening, with one board member signalling scope for faster increases.
The Australian dollar strengthened 0.09% versus the greenback to US$0.701, while New Zealand's kiwi climbed 0.12% to US$0.5627.
In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin gained 0.60% to US$80,660.59, and ether rose 0.45% to US$2,428.15.
8b0ceab9fdc99f0a: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — The Ministry of Defence is in the final stages of evaluating three options for a surface-to-surface missile (SSM) system after the Norwegian government cancelled the export permit for the Naval Strike Missile (NSM).
The ministry said the selection of the system would take into account operational requirements, integration compatibility with naval vessels, costs and the procurement timeline.

“A final decision will be made once an option has been agreed upon and the procurement agreement has been signed,” the ministry said in a written reply to an oral question from Datuk Wira Dr Ku Abd Rahman Ku Ismail (PN-Kubang Pasu) in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday.

He had asked Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin to state the government’s measures to obtain the NSM system from another country following the Norwegian government’s cancellation of the export permit.

In a related development, the overall physical progress of the construction of all five Royal Malaysian Navy (RMN) Littoral Combat Ships (LCS) stood at 80.72 per cent as of Sept 25, representing a delay variance of 9.19 per cent against the original target of 89.91 per cent.

According to the ministry, the latest delivery schedule guaranteed by the contractor, Lumut Naval Shipyard (LUNAS), stipulates that the first LCS will be delivered in April 2027, followed by the second in August 2027 and the third in December 2027.
The fourth LCS is scheduled for delivery in August 2028, while the fifth is set for April 2029.
As for the first LCS, KD Maharaja Lela, the vessel is currently undergoing Harbour Acceptance Trials after completing several shipyard acceptance tests.

The ministry said the trials involve testing the main machinery, power generation and propulsion systems to evaluate and verify the vessel’s performance and system capabilities before the Sea Acceptance Trials (SAT) are conducted together with RMN. — Bernama

2e1e8affa47e6ae8: LONDON: Gold prices rose in early Asian trade on Thursday after posting their biggest daily gain since mid-August in the previous session, buoyed by a weaker US dollar, while investors awaited this week's non-farm payrolls report for clues on the Federal Reserve's policy outlook.
Spot gold was up 0.6 per cent at US$4,082.76 per ounce by 0036 GMT, after climbing about 3.4 per cent on Monday. US gold futures for December delivery gained 0.5 per cent to US$4,092.90.

The dollar retreated on Wednesday but was off its earlier lows after a sweeping victory by Democrats in the US midterm elections removed a source of uncertainty for the market while investors gauged the potential for regulatory changes.
A weaker dollar makes greenback-priced bullion more affordable for holders of other currencies.
US private payrolls growth increased further in October, the ADP National Employment Report showed on Wednesday.
Market participants now await the US nonfarm payrolls report on Friday to further gauge the Federal Reserve's monetary policy outlook.

On the geopolitical front, Washington's hostility towards Tehran will not change through partisan shifts or any concessions to the US, and those who believe otherwise are "greatly mistaken", Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said on Wednesday.
Traders currently see an 83 per cent chance that the Fed will raise rates in December, according to CME's FedWatch tool.
Higher interest rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion, reducing its appeal to investors.

Meanwhile, Citi has a 0-3 month price target of US$4,500 per ounce for gold, it said on Wednesday, as it sees substantial upside potential if the Strait of Hormuz reopens and the Yemen/Saudi conflict de-escalates by the year-end, as it expects.

Euro zone inflation rose to a three-year high last month on surging food and energy costs and was set to rise further in the coming months, firming up the case for another European Central Bank rate hike in December.
The Bank of England is widely expected to raise interest rates for the first time in three years on Thursday due to mounting inflation pressures from the US-Iran war.
Among other metals, spot silver rose 0.3 per cent to US$52.37 per ounce, platinum gained 0.6 per cent to US$1,505.85 and palladium dropped 0.1 per cent to US$1,003.83.
69185f787d5d95a7: KUALA LUMPUR: It will be a Deepavali to forget for S. Sivasangari, after her US Open campaign ended in a quarter-final defeat to world champion Amina Orfi of Egypt on Wednesday.
The world No. 4 had been looking forward to getting the better of Orfi, but was outclassed 11-8, 11-1, 11-8 in 43 minutes in Philadelphia.
