World No. 1 Orfi, who has won the London Classic, Qatar Classic and Egyptian Open this year, will face compatriot Nour El Sherbini or American Amanda Sobhy in the semi-finals tomorrow.
Squash Racquets Association of Malaysia coaching director Andrew Cross said Sivasangari had done her best, but Orfi was simply better.
The 27-year-old Sivasangari, who won the Silicon Valley Open last month, will now turn her attention to the China Open from Nov 17-22.
Orfi said she knew she would face a tough test, having lost to Sivasangari twice this year.
"I prepared well as I knew Sivasangari would be confident going into the match, especially after becoming the first in women's squash to qualify for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
"Sivasangari is definitely a threat to everyone on the tour as she has beaten the best.
"But today, I stepped onto the court with a game plan, and I am happy it worked," Orfi told PSA Squash Tour.
2fcc721602c091f8: JOHOR BAHRU: Police have confirmed that the six-year-old boy who was found unconscious in a retention pond near Taman Sungai Mas in Kulai yesterday died from drowning.
Kulai district police chief Tan Seng Lee said the boy was believed to have gone fishing at the pond, located about 50m from his home.
"Preliminary investigations revealed that the victim’s parents left for work at about 6.30am while the boy and his 17-year-old sister were still asleep.
"At about 10am, an acquaintance told the victim’s mother that her son had been found unconscious in the pond," he said in a statement today.
Tan said a fishing rod was also found near the scene.
He said the boy was pronounced dead at 11.15am by a medical officer from Kulai Hospital after firefighters retrieved him from the pond.
Tan said a post-mortem examination confirmed drowning as the cause of death.
Police found no signs of foul play at the scene and have classified the case as sudden death, with investigations ongoing.

Tan urged parents and guardians to keep a close watch on their children and ensure that they do not engage in activities near ponds, rivers or other potentially dangerous bodies of water without adult supervision.
c0e20b4c834f9bf9: PARIS: The cooling system of France's blood bank has been hit by a cyberattack similar to the hacker attack targeting refrigeration systems across Europe earlier this week, the EFS bank said on Wednesday, reported German Press Agency (dpa).
Cooling rooms in three of the bank's locations have been affected, EFS said.
The refrigeration systems, supplied by an external provider, were manipulated remotely, causing operating temperatures to rise to very high levels, it said.
Temperatures rose from -30 degrees Celsius to plus 11 degrees, according to investigative newspaper Le Canard Enchaîné.
Thanks to the monitoring and alarm systems, the rise in temperature had been detected quickly and action was taken swiftly. No samples or blood products have been compromised, according to EFS.
The affected systems have since been brought under control again, and blood products have been transferred to other facilities as a precautionary measure, it said.
The EFS stores blood products and bio samples, which are kept in cooling units before delivery to healthcare facilities.

It comes after cybercriminals targeted fridges and freezers in European supermarkets, causing them to become warmer, including in Belgium, Sweden, Ireland, Luxembourg, Estonia, Finland, Germany and the Netherlands.
A similar, large-scale attack in mid-October caused fridges to go warm in large French supermarket chains.
It remains unclear who was behind the attacks.
993bc96e3c72d7f6: MEXICO CITY: Pixar Animation Studios said on Wednesday that veteran Jonathan Garson will become president on Jan 4, replacing Jim Morris, who will step back from day-to-day leadership ahead of his eventual retirement.

Pixar is part of the Disney empire, which bought the animation studio in 2006 and brought the maker of "Toy Story" and "The Incredibles" under the same corporate roof as Disney's own animation business.

The reshuffle sets up the next generation of leadership at Pixar, with Garson taking charge of production and operations while Chief Creative Officer Pete Docter retains oversight of the studio's films, the studio said.
Morris, Pixar's president for 12 years, will step back to take the president emeritus role and remain involved in "Incredibles 3" and other projects.
Garson has been with Pixar since 2010 and with Disney for more than 30 years. He most recently served as Pixar's general manager.
Morris joined Pixar in 2005 and has served as president for 12 years, with Pixar saying its feature films generated more than US$12 billion at the global box office during his tenure.
Pixar's upcoming slate includes "Gatto" in March 2027, "Ghost Market" in March 2028 and "Incredibles 3" in June 2028.
6ba1b996981c9aba: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Two Special Branch policemen have filed a civil lawsuit against Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain, suing him in his personal capacity for alleged assault, battery, false imprisonment, and defamation following an altercation at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA).

Lance Corporals Muhammad Ekmal Sofwan Dirman and Mohamad Faiz Muhamad Saman initiated the tort action at the Sepang Sessions Court yesterday, naming the border agency chief as the sole defendant while excluding the federal government from the suit, NST reported.
Their counsel, Kamal Hisham Ja'afar and Muhammad Nor Tamrin, confirmed that the action pursues general, special, exemplary, and aggravated damages.

The civil lawsuit escalates the legal scrutiny surrounding Shuhaily, who was charged at the Sepang Magistrate's Court on Oct 21 with two criminal counts of voluntarily causing hurt under Section 323 of the Penal Code. Shuhaily pleaded not guilty to both charges and remains out on court bail.

According to the statement of claim, both plaintiffs were deployed as Travel Control Officers at KLIA Terminal 1 on Sept 28, tasked with security surveillance during Shuhaily's working visit to inspect border entry protocols for arriving Formula One contingents.
At around 1.27pm, the officers allegedly witnessed Shuhaily angrily confronting a civilian during a document check inside an enclosed inspection area near Counter J on Level 5.

Faiz captured photographs of the incident for internal intelligence logs, prompting MCBA deputy director-general for operations Datuk Mohd Nasaruddin M. Nasir to seize the mobile phone before escorting both policemen directly to Shuhaily.

The plaintiffs alleged that upon discovering they were Special Branch personnel, Shuhaily grew incensed, questioned why police intelligence was monitoring MCBA personnel, and initiated a physical confrontation.

In their pleadings, the plaintiffs alleged that Shuhaily headbutted Ekmal four times before turning on Faiz, grabbing both of his ears and violently shaking his head, an ordeal that left them terrified and fearing for their physical safety.

The lawsuit also targets statements made by Shuhaily during a media briefing on Oct 1, accusing him of defaming the two officers by publicly implying that they had deliberately sabotaged border operations and recorded the altercation to tarnish the reputation of the agency and its leadership.
The plaintiffs contended that the remarks damaged their professional integrity and caused severe distress among their peers and families.
e534448c802906ea: ISTANBUL, Nov 5— Dirk Kuyt got the better of his former club Liverpool as Fenerbahce twice came from behind for a famous 3-2 win in Istanbul yesterday that breathed new life into their Champions League campaign.
Liverpool had won their opening three European games under Andoni Iraola, but were punished for sloppy defending in a surprise defeat.
Trey Nyoni and substitute Alexander Isak twice put the visitors in front.
But Liverpool, who lost twice away to Galatasaray last season, were beaten again in Istanbul as Englishmen Mason Greenwood and Archie Brown levelled before Vedat Muriqi’s winner.
“We’ve gone twice in front after having good moments, controlling the game, we’ve found the goals but after we’ve conceded in situations we should definitely defend better,” said Iraola.
Fenerbahce’s interim boss Kuyt, who spent six years at Anfield as a player, was taking charge for just the second time after Ismail Kartal quit last week.
The Turkish giants had taken just two points from their opening three Champions League games but made the most of Liverpool’s generosity at the back.
Liverpool’s perfect Champions League start allowed Iraola the luxury of leaving out Isak and Florian Wirtz among five changes from Sunday’s 1-0 defeat by Arsenal.
Nyoni retained his place and capped another fine performance with his first Liverpool goal from the edge of the box after Fenerbahce failed to clear Dominik Szoboszlai’s cross.
The home side bounced back just four minutes later when Alisson Becker was deceived by Greenwood’s deflected free-kick to equalise.
Iraola unleashed Isak, Wirtz and Cody Gakpo from the bench just after the hour mark in search of a winner and got an almost immediate reward.
Isak was afforded far too much space to head in Gakpo’s cross.
But again Liverpool quickly handed back their advantage.
Gakpo’s touch inadvertently deflected a cross beyond Alisson to give Brown an easy tap-in at the back post.
Liverpool then conceded for the 10th time in four Champions League games when Muriqi outmuscled Jeremy Jacquet to a looping cross and steered a header into the bottom corner.
Defeat cost Liverpool the chance to move level with Paris Saint-Germain at the top of the Champions League table.

“I think we’ve put ourselves in good positions, so that today if we lose this game it’s not a chaos situation,” said Isak. “We just need to get back to winning ways and if we win the next game, we are back to a really good position.”
Victory moves Fenerbahce move up to 19th in the 36-team table.
Only the top eight qualify directly for the last 16 with ninth to 24th facing off in a two-legged play-off. — AFP
a9444e2735884a79: SUBANG JAYA, Nov 5 — Getting siew yoke right is harder than it looks. At The Roast Meat Shop in Sunway Geo, Harry Fong found that achieving crisp crackling was only part of the challenge; getting it consistently crisp across an entire piece of roast pork was another matter.

“One of our biggest challenges was translating our home-cooking recipes into something that could be prepared consistently in a restaurant,” Fong says. “It took me about half a year of recipe development, ingredient sourcing and repeated testing to find the right ingredients and combinations for our siew yoke and char siew.”

“Some sections would turn out beautifully crispy, while others would not crackle properly. Sometimes, the skin would even become rubbery after a while. We had to keep experimenting and refining our roasting process to improve the consistency.”
The shop’s signature siew yoke uses a marinade combining Western and traditional herbs, followed by a traditional roasting method.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
The Roast Meat Shop in Sunway Geo is run by Harry Fong and his wife Olivia Yap. — Picture courtesy of The Roast Meat Shop
“We want our siew yoke to have its own distinctive taste,” Fong says. “We want every part of the skin to achieve that satisfying crackling while keeping the meat succulent.”

Before opening the restaurant, Fong spent more than a decade as a country manager for a German company. He had always enjoyed cooking and dreamed of owning a restaurant. His wife, Olivia Yap, shared his love of roast meats: she favoured char siew, while he preferred siew yoke.
“We started experimenting with roasting meat at home, trying different ingredients and techniques until we began developing recipes we were happy with,” Fong says.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
The Roast Meat Shop in Sunway Geo is run by Harry Fong and his wife Olivia Yap. — Picture courtesy of The Roast Meat Shop
For Yap, the menu also carries memories of family and childhood.
“One dish that is especially meaningful to me is our sour-and-spicy Chinese mustard roast pork,” she says. “My grandmother was Hakka, and this was one of the dishes we enjoyed at home.”

Yap recalls how her mother would cook it after Chinese New Year celebrations or other special Chinese festivals: “The recipe was passed down from my grandmother, so bringing it into our restaurant is a way for me to share a little of our family heritage with our customers.”
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Yap favoured 'char siew', while Fong preferred 'siew yoke.' — Picture courtesy of The Roast Meat Shop

Another dish, the Blessing Dumplings, comes from Yap’s aunt, who lives in the United States and makes them when she returns home. Her aunt learned the recipe more than 30 years ago at a Chinese restaurant in Chinatown.
“I still remember eating those dumplings when I was a little girl. The meat was so juicy that I told myself, ‘I must learn this recipe from her when I grow up!’” Yap says.
Adapting these family recipes for a restaurant took repeated testing.
“We failed a few times because achieving the same taste we were familiar with at home became much more challenging when cooking in larger quantities,” Yap explains.
After several attempts and adjustments, the couple established standard operating procedures to maintain consistency.
The Blessing Dumplings needed further refinement after customers said the skin was initially too thick. Yap searched for an alternative, although the new supplier charged more.

“I still remember my husband asking whether we should switch to a new supplier because the cost was higher than what we were paying previously,” she says. “We knew that getting the right dumpling skin was important to the overall experience.”
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
The recipe for their sour-and-spicy Chinese mustard roast pork was passed down from Yap’s grandmother. — Picture courtesy of The Roast Meat Shop
The same attention to detail shapes the rest of the menu. The couple draw on food they enjoy at home rather than adding dishes simply to offer more choice.
“We don't want to introduce a dish simply to offer more choices,” Yap says. “We want to be confident that every dish we serve is something we would be happy to eat ourselves.”

The shop’s best-selling wantan noodles are one example. “Getting the house-made sauce right didn't happen overnight. We collected feedback from diners and made several adjustments to the recipe before settling on a version we were happy with,” she says.
The couple use duck egg noodles for their firm, springy or “QQ” texture and because they lack a strong alkaline taste.
“The cost of making the sauce is higher, but we feel it is worth it,” Yap says. “For us, flavour and quality matter more than simply choosing the cheapest ingredients.”

The couple prepare their food in-house daily. Fong oversees operations, from the kitchen to the front of house, while Yap focuses on the back-end and marketing, including promotions, customer engagement and Chinese New Year vacuum-packed roast meat hampers.

“We have different responsibilities, but we discuss ideas and make important business decisions together,” Yap says. “We listen to each other's views and try to find a way forward that works for the business.”
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
The Blessing Dumplings. — Picture courtesy of The Roast Meat Shop
Maintaining quality also means making careful decisions about suppliers, staffing and the details of each meal.
“We pay close attention to ingredient costs and explore different suppliers to find the best value without compromising on quality,” Fong says.
The shop’s noodle and rice dishes come with small side servings of onsen egg and Japanese cucumber. Removing them would cut costs, but Fong believes they contribute to a more complete meal.

“There are times when maintaining our standards means accepting a smaller profit margin. We could cut certain items or take shortcuts to reduce costs, but we believe these small details contribute to the overall dining experience,” he says.

The couple are also developing vacuum-packed roast meats for customers to enjoy at home. Meanwhile, a second restaurant is in the planning stage, with decisions to make about location, operating costs, equipment, staffing and ingredient supplies.

One option is to turn the first outlet into a central kitchen, with roasting and food preparation done there before supplies are sent to the second restaurant. The couple are training potential staff and looking for suitable candidates, including a kitchen leader who can help maintain standards.
“Ultimately, we want to expand in a structured and sustainable manner, making sure we have the right people, systems, and processes in place before taking the next step,” Fong says.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Duck egg noodles are used for their 'QQ' texture and lack of a strong alkaline taste. — Picture courtesy of The Roast Meat Shop
Running a restaurant has required sacrifices, including personal time, rest and financial security. Yet the couple measure success by more than sales or the number of outlets they operate.
“To us, success means building a sustainable business with a strong reputation, maintaining the quality and consistency of our food, and earning the trust and loyalty of our customers,” Yap says.

“Most importantly, we want The Roast Meat Shop to grow without losing its identity or compromising the principles that we started with. We would rather expand at the right pace than grow too quickly at the expense of quality.”
As Yap puts it, “We started because we love good food and wanted to share it with others.”
The Roast Meat Shop

Subang Jaya, Selangor.
Open daily 10.30am–8.30pm

ad3501d58c1e1f39: BERLIN, Nov 5 — A prominent German politician was found dead in a Berlin hotel yesterday, police said, adding they had launched an investigation.
The cause of death of Hubert Aiwanger, 55, who was deputy leader of southern Bavaria state, was not immediately clear.
Police in the capital said in a statement he was “found dead in his hotel room” in the Berlin-Mitte district.
Police and prosecutors had opened a probe to “determine the specific cause and circumstances of death and to rule out any possible involvement of third parties”, the statement said.

Aiwanger, head of the populist Free Voters party and also Bavarian economy minister, was in Berlin to attend the opening of an office for his party but missed the event as he was feeling unwell, the Bild daily reported.
His body was later discovered by police in the hotel, it said.
Bavarian state premier Markus Soeder described his death as an “absolute tragedy”.
“We are all deeply shocked. Our thoughts are now first and foremost with his family and his children,” he said.
Aiwanger’s party were junior partners in the regional Bavarian government led by Soeder’s Christian Social Union (CSU).
He had headed the Bavarian branch of the Free Voters since 2006. Under his leadership, the party made it into the state government for the first time in 2018.
He had faced national controversy in 2023 after it emerged that Nazi pamphlets were found in his schoolbag as a teenager in the late 1980s.
He apologised over the affair but refused to step down.
Aiwanger had two children and lived with his partner, German media reported. — AFP
2718a679250f3f9a: WASHINGTON, Nov 5 — While Republicans nursed a brutal hangover from their US midterms defeat, President Donald Trump was busy—showing off his new ballroom at the White House.
“It’s going to be not only one of the biggest, but it’ll be the most beautiful ballroom I think anywhere in the world,” Trump told reporters inside the skeleton of the building.
It was a surreal start to one of Trump’s most surreal press conferences.

Instead of the formal post-midterms remarks that previous presidents have made, the 80-year-old announced that he was there to sign the final steel beam going into the roof of his US$400 million pride and joy.
He followed up with an extraordinary, 16-minute speech on everything from marble to kitchen layouts to drones.
“Now envision chandeliers all over the ceiling,” the former real estate magnate sighed, speaking against a backdrop of a huge American flag. “Envision marble floors.”
Absent from the billionaire president’s monologue was any mention of the stinging rebuke from US voters angered by the Iran war and the cost of living.
'Creme de la creme'

And while reporters waited to question him on how he would govern when Democrats take control of Congress, Trump kept talking about how the ballroom’s classical columns would dwarf those of the US Supreme Court.
“They’re being carved out of beautiful limestone, and they’ll be Corinthian—the Corinthian design which is considered the creme de la creme,” said Trump.
Then he was on to the marble floors.
“It’s a vein that people have been after for 50 years, and the owner of the quarry didn’t want to sell it, but he liked me,” he touted.

He wasn’t finished. Trump also wanted to talk about the roof of the building, which he said could hold up to 100 drones, or a number of helicopters, and how Chinese President Xi had admired the structure when he visited the White House in September.
Was this all a sign of what Trump actually intends to spend his time doing in his remaining two years in office?
It certainly looked like it—not least because it echoed Trump’s election-eve press conference on Monday to reopen the refurbished Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, which critics derided as tone-deaf.
Day of celebration
Afterwards, it was US Interior Secretary Doug Burgum’s turn to speak.
“Today, of course, is a day of celebration, and it’s a day of gratitude,” Burgum said—a day after Democrats seized both the House of Representatives and Senate from Republicans.
Reality intruded when Trump finally took questions from reporters at the construction site, but anyone expecting a Trump-style tantrum was to be disappointed.

The president was remarkably sanguine about the election results, and wasn’t even moved by Vice President JD Vance’s earlier statement that the Iran war was the “reason we lost,” an apparent break with the president by a likely candidate for the 2028 election.
“I think it’s largely true because it drove the gasoline up a little bit short term,” Trump said.
The president then fielded a few questions on whether he would work with Democrats, and warned them against trying to impeach him for a third time.
“Our country is more successful right now than at any time in its history,” he said, before breaking off in mid-sentence and pointing to the ceiling.
“Watch the beam go up,” he told the press. — AFP
aaa63ac4bdcbefca: KUALA LUMPUR: Many young Hindus grow up seeing flowers offered at a shrine, leaves used in rituals or certain foods prepared for prayer. Yet knowing what those items are called, and why they matter, is another question altogether.
A new four-volume collection hopes to bridge that gap by documenting the objects, plants, foods and practices that have long formed part of Hindu worship and household traditions.

Published in Tamil, English and Sanskrit, “Sri Shaankari Parampara - A Sacred Legacy for the Next Generation” brings together information on pooja items, leaves, flowers, herbs, spices, traditional foods and rituals used in homes and temples.
The collection was authored by Sri Shankara Vijayendra Saraswathi Swamigal, the 70th Jagadguru Shankaracharya, or spiritual head, of Sri Kanchi Kamakoti Peetham in Kanchipuram, Tamil Nadu.

Sri Muthumariamman Thirukoil Devasthanam trustee Gunaseelan Palanivello said the books were intended not simply as religious texts, but as practical references for people who may recognise the traditions around them without fully understanding their significance.
“These are a valuable guide for Generation Z and for many of us who come across these items but may not know their names or purpose,” he said at a media preview at the Royal Lake Club recently.
The collection also traces the spiritual lineage and teachings of eighth-century philosopher and monk Sri Adi Shankara, while explaining the role of traditional practices in worship and daily life.
It includes scientific names for plants and ingredients, alongside references to traditional health benefits and concepts associated with ayurveda and the doshas.
“The books are a beautifully illustrated Vedic encyclopedia documenting sacred Hindu traditions to help readers identify familiar worship items and understand their purpose.
“Through beautiful colour photographs on glossy pages, this collection helps us recognise the various items and practices and better understand their significance," Gunaseelan said.
Copies of the collection, officially launched on Oct 30, will be distributed to Hindu organisations, temples and Tamil schools, where they can be used by students, teachers and the wider community.

Among the subjects covered in the books are 97 forms of traditional "neivedyam" - food or other offerings made to a Hindu deity - and "prasadam", the consecrated food later received by devotees as a blessing.
Gunaseelan said these sections are intended to connect practices familiar from temples and family prayer with the broader traditions of "sanatana dharma".
“These introduce readers to the rich botanical knowledge embedded in our traditions and the way plants have been valued in traditional approaches to health and well-being,” he added.
For him, the books are especially useful because younger generations may have access to more information than ever before, yet still lack the ability to start looking for it.

“Our children can scroll the internet for almost anything, but they cannot search for knowledge they do not know exists. This encyclopaedia gives them the vocabulary, images and understanding of our own heritage.”

He stressed that while the internet can deepen that knowledge, a physical reference offers families a starting point to which they could return together - "a lasting resource to hold, explore and share as a family".
Gunaseelan also noted that older members of the community have an important role to play in ensuring such knowledge is not lost between generations.

“As parents, guardians, teachers and leaders, we have a shared duty to pass our heritage to the next generation with care and urgency. Let us give our children both roots to cherish and knowledge to carry forward," he said.
To get your copy of the books, contact Gunaseelan at 011-1132 5978.
1cf5c0a6a8a8fc1b: PETALING JAYA: Membangkitkan isu institusi Melayu untuk memburuk-burukkan Umno dan Barisan Nasional (BN) tidak banyak membantu Pakatan Harapan (PH) meraih undi pada PRN Melaka, kata seorang penganalisis.
Serangan peribadi terhadap calon lawan juga dilihat tidak mampu membawa hasil, kata seorang lagi penganalisis politik.
“PH boleh berkempen selantang dan seagresif di Melaka seperti dalam PRN sebelum ini, asalkan berhati-hati apabila melibatkan institusi Melayu,” kata Azmi Hassan daripada Akademi Nusantara kepada FMT.
Beliau menekankan, serangan agresif PH terhadap Umno berkait isu Tabung Haji (TH) pada kempen Negeri Sembilan gagal menarik minat pengundi.
“Saya rasa pengundi Melayu menolak PH sebahagiannya disebabkan pendekatan agresifnya serta cubaan mengaitkan Umno dengan kegagalan TH, Felda, dan UiTM Holdings,” katanya.

Azmi berkata, persepsi terus menyelubungi orang Melayu mengenai DAP dituduh cuba 'memusnahkan' TH apabila kerajaan menubuhkan syarikat bertujuan khas (SPV) Urusharta Jamaah Sdn Bhd pada 2018, bagi menguruskan pengambilalihan aset TH yang kurang berprestasi.
Hal berkenaan berlaku sewaktu tempoh perkhidmatan Lim Guan Eng sebagai menteri kewangan. Lim juga merupakan setiausaha agung DAP ketika itu.

Laporan suruhanjaya siasatan diraja dikeluarkan pada Ogos, mendedahkan tadbir urus lemah, campur tangan politik, dan pelaporan kewangan mengelirukan menjurus TH melaporkan keuntungan RM3.4 bilion walaupun mengalami defisit RM11 bilion, dari 2014 hingga 2020.

Bagi Felda pula, kerajaan mendedahkan pengurusan kewangan lemah, pengambilalihan korporat secara agresif, dan campur tangan politik mengakibatkan kerugian RM10 bilion pada 2017, manakala UiTM mencatatkan kerugian sebelum cukai RM157 juta bagi tempoh empat tahun bermula 2017.
“Saya fikir anda perlu bersuara lantang dan agresif (dalam kempen Melaka), tetapi bukannya menyerang (Umno-BN) secara langsung menggunakan isu institusi Melayu. Ia tidak berkesan,” kata Azmi.
Katanya, PH Melaka sepatutnya memberi tumpuan meyakinkan pengundi gabungan itu mampu mentadbir lebih baik berbanding BN.

Beliau mengulas kenyataan terbaru Setiausaha Agung PH Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, bahawa gabungan itu akan menjalankan kempen secara aman bagi PRN Melaka, selepas insaf kemenangan bukannya milik mereka yang paling lantang, sebaliknya milik pihak yang paling dipercayai.

Kenyataan Saifuddin itu dibuat ketika PH melangkah ke kempen PRN yang keempat sejak penghujung tahun lalu — menyusuli PRN di Sabah, Johor, dan Negeri Sembilan — dengan kejayaan pilihan raya kurang memberangsangkan.
PH hanya menang satu daripada lima kerusi ditandingi pada PRN Sabah, November tahun lalu, merosot berbanding lapan kerusi pada PRN 2020.

Dalam PRN Johor Julai lalu, gabungan tersebut menang lapan kerusi, merosot daripada 12 kerusi disandang, manakala pada PRN Negeri Sembilan pada Ogos, ia hanya menang 11 kawasan berbanding 17 kerusi pada pilihan raya 2023.
Elak serang peribadi
Pakar akademik Lau Zhe Wei daripada Universiti Islam Antarabangsa Malaysia, berkata PH mesti mengelak kempen membuat serangan peribadi terhadap calon lawan.
Perkara itu cukup relevan terutama melibatkan penyandang berprestasi baik, seperti calon BN, Noor Helmy Abdul Halem, yang berharap menang penggal kedua sebagai Adun Duyong, katanya kepada FMT.

“Helmy popular dalam kalangan penduduk Duyong, termasuk bukan Melayu. Jika anda terus-menerus mengkritik lawan, ia akan menimbulkan tindak balas negatif,” katanya sambil menambah PH sepatutnya menyerang parti dan bukan calon.
PH bertanding 24 daripada 28 kerusi pada PRN Melaka 14 Nov.
5313efaed0709fba: PETALING JAYA: An analyst sees Barisan Nasional’s (BN) willingness to offer Perikatan Nasional (PN) positions in the Melaka government if it wins the state election as a long-term "political investment" to build stronger cooperation ahead of the 16th general election (GE16).
Tawfik Yaakub said PN’s participation in the state government would not be necessary from a numbers perspective if BN secured a comfortable majority, particularly a two-thirds majority.
Instead, he said the offer showed that BN wanted to build ties with PN beyond electoral cooperation, including ensuring the transfer of votes between supporters of both coalitions.

"It is also a signal that the BN-PN understanding is not merely electoral cooperation but could potentially develop into a power-sharing arrangement in government," the Universiti Malaya academic told FMT.
BN is contesting 23 of the 28 seats in the Nov 14 Melaka election while PN is fielding candidates in the remaining five constituencies.
Last Sunday, BN chairman Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said BN would allocate roles in the Melaka executive council to PN if their alliance succeeds in winning the state election.
Tawfik said PN assemblymen could also be appointed as the state assembly speaker or deputy speaker, or to government-linked companies and local authorities.
However, he said the power-sharing arrangement could raise questions among Umno grassroots members, especially if BN was capable of forming the government on its own.
He said the arrangement could also trigger competition for influence, including over the allocation of portfolios and management of state political resources.
"Zahid’s main challenge is to ensure that the understanding among the coalition’s leaders is also accepted by the grassroots," he said.

Mazlan Ali of Universiti Teknologi Malaysia said while BN had the strength to dominate Melaka and form the government on its own, cooperation with PN was important in the broader political contest ahead of GE16.
He said BN wanted to leverage PN’s influence, particularly that of PAS, to help mobilise Malay voters and give Umno an advantage amid several controversies.
These include issues involving Tabung Haji and donations to pay the fine imposed on former prime minister Najib Razak, which was a requirement for his conditional pardon.
"It has shaken the confidence of the Malays… and Umno needs PN’s support to retain their votes," he said.
Mazlan said the cooperation was also driven by Umno’s desire to maintain the narrative of "Muslim unity" which, according to him, would be difficult to achieve without PAS.
"In Melaka, Zahid is opening the door to PN to safeguard relations for the future," he said.
5d492cb4a85604f9: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — The 2026 Cyber Crime Bill provides powers for the court to issue property restriction orders to prevent scam proceeds from being dissipated, even before a suspect has been charged.

Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the provision under clause 54 enables the court to issue orders to prevent or stop violations of the law, thereby protecting victims of cybercrime.

“Among the orders that can be issued include cessation orders, restitution orders to victims, compliance orders, and property restriction orders to prevent assets such as scam proceeds from being dissipated,” he said in a written Dewan Rakyat reply yesterday.
He said that applications to obtain such orders can be submitted by the Public Prosecutor or an authorised officer.

Ahmad Zahid, who is also the Minister of Rural and Regional Development, said the Bill - passed by Parliament last July - was formulated to tackle online scams utilising artificial intelligence (AI), including identity impersonation, deepfakes, and digital manipulation.

He was answering a question from Datuk Shamshulkahar Mohd Deli (BN-Jempol) regarding the adequacy of the existing legal framework to handle AI-based online fraud, as well as specific reinforced provisions to accelerate actions against syndicates and protect victims. — Bernama
0e4a925590b32897: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof has clarified that his presence in Melaka today was strictly on official business and has no connection to the state’s political developments.

Fadillah, who is also Energy Transition and Water Transformation Minister, said his visit was to officiate the 2026 CGNEI Gas Turbine Power Generation Committee Annual Conference at the EPH Training Centre, Edra Melaka Power Plant, in Kuala Sungai Baru.
In a statement yesterday, he said the conference is an energy generation programme that benefits the state’s economy and national energy security.

He noted that the conference, also attended by Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, is an initiative by CGN Energy International (CGNEI) and Edra Power Holdings Sdn Bhd through the establishment of the CGNEI Gas Turbine Skills Training Centre (CGNEI GTSTC) in Melaka.
“Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh’s presence at the event was also in his capacity as Chief Minister upon invitation by the organisers,” Fadillah said.
The statement was issued to set the record straight following attempts by certain quarters to link his presence at the event to current political developments in the state. — Bernama
83509aac5680decf: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 5 — Hospital Seberang Jaya (HSJ) has made history as the first Level 2 hospital in Peninsular Malaysia to offer angiogram and angioplasty procedures, expanding access to specialised cardiac care for residents of Seberang Perai and surrounding areas.

Congratulating the hospital’s staff, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the expansion of services is expected to shorten waiting times and reduce the need for patients to seek treatment at Penang Hospital (HPP).

“Last January, I visited HSJ to officiate the hospital’s new building. Today’s development is certainly pleasing, as the upgraded facilities have now been followed by the expansion of specialised treatment urgently needed by residents in Seberang Perai and surrounding areas.

“My highest appreciation goes to the doctors, nurses, healthcare personnel, hospital management, and the Health Ministry (MOH) for this achievement. Your expertise and service bring hope to patients and strengthen public confidence in the country’s public healthcare sector,” he posted on social media last night.

Anwar said the Madani Government will continue to enhance the capabilities of public hospitals so that more people can receive faster access to quality treatment to protect lives and the people’s wellbeing.

Meanwhile, Penang State Cardiology Services head Datuk Dr Mohamed Jahangir Abdul Wahab said the operation of HSJ’s Invasive Cardiology Laboratory, which enables coronary angiogram and angioplasty procedures, reflects the government’s commitment to widening access to quality healthcare.
Dr Mohamed Jahangir, who is also HPP’s Cardiology Department head, said the initiative follows efforts by the Prime Minister and MOH to ensure more citizens have access to necessary specialised care.
According to him, the primary goal of expanding the service is to ensure patients receive quality cardiac care promptly and closer to home, without enduring long waits.
“With the rising burden of cardiovascular disease and the demand for increasingly complex cardiac care, expanding adult cardiology services at HSJ is a significant strategic step,” he told Bernama.

Dr Mohamed Jahangir said long-term plans are in place to develop HSJ into a more comprehensive heart treatment centre, which will include managing complex adult cardiology cases and introducing cardiothoracic surgical services targeted by mid-2027.

He said the initiative will not only increase cardiac treatment capacity in Penang, but also position HSJ as another major cardiovascular referral centre for the northern region of Peninsular Malaysia.

The development of adult cardiology services at HSJ has been carried out in phases since 2023, beginning with the posting of a resident cardiologist before being strengthened through regular specialist rotations, culminating in the establishment of the Cardiology Unit.

The unit is currently equipped with four Coronary Care Unit (CCU) beds and 15 Coronary Rehabilitation Ward (CRW) beds, alongside an Invasive Cardiology Laboratory fitted with an angiography system and modern electrophysiology equipment. — Bernama
e9940f0b094ff177: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — The quality of RON95 petrol samples, mitigation of solid waste landfills, and enforcement against foreigners driving without valid licences are among the key issues slated for discussion in the Dewan Rakyat today.

According to the Order Paper on the Parliament portal, Abdul Latiff Abdul Rahman (PN-Kuala Krai) will ask the Minister of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living to state the analysis outcome of RON95 samples across five states and depots during the Minister’s Question Time.
He is also seeking information on the government’s immediate measures to restore consumer confidence and the compensation for affected vehicle owners.

In the same session, Datuk Dr Richard Rapu @ Aman Begri (GPS-Betong) will ask the Ministry of Housing and Local Government about the long-term strategy for critical open dumpsites under rural local authorities (PBT), as well as mitigation plans for districts without Waste-to-Energy (WTE) plants to curb daily waste accumulation.

Siti Mastura Muhammad (PN-Kepala Batas) is scheduled to ask the Transport Minister to elaborate on enforcement mechanisms against foreigners, including United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) cardholders and undocumented immigrants driving motor vehicles without a valid licence, during the oral question-and-answer session.

Datuk Seri Hasni Mohammad (BN-Simpang Renggam) is scheduled to ask the Home Minister to state the progress of the early detection radar system, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV), and satellite systems, the percentage of 24-hour surveillance coverage, and the asset capability gaps of the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) that remain critical.

Rodiyah Sapiee (GPS-Batang Sadong) is also scheduled to ask about the government’s preparedness measures to prevent and address haze episodes, as the El Nino phenomenon is expected to persist until mid-2027.

At the conclusion of the question-and-answer session, the Dewan Rakyat will continue with the committee stage debate and ministerial replies for the Supply (Budget) Bill 2027 and the Motion on the 2027 Development Expenditure Estimates.

4632fc754eec2b40: WASHINGTON, Nov 5 —Has MAGA fever finally broken? Will the American right shed Donald Trump’s populist ideology and return to more traditional conservatism?
After a resounding defeat in midterm elections that were all about one man, many Republicans on Wednesday are questioning the party’s future—and the role, if any, of President Trump in shaping it.

The Wall Street Journal, whose opinion pages are the standard-bearer of the establishment right, has demanded “soul-searching” and called for a break with the ultranationalist, identity-based rhetoric that fueled the octogenarian’s rise to power.

“Tariffs and mass deportation are no substitute for rising real incomes. Playing to the bro MAGA base is no substitute for persuading Hispanics, independents and suburban swing voters who abandoned the party on Tuesday,” the Journal’s editorial board wrote Wednesday morning.
Still your president
The White House was in a less reflective mood.
Its first X post yesterdayfeatured a stern-looking Trump with the words “Trump is still your president” superimposed on it—a reminder he can remain in office until January 2029.
But the American political cycle is relentless. Yesterdayeffectively marks the kickoff of the 2028 campaign, which will culminate in a vote on Trump’s successor.
And in this race, Trump is out for good, since the US Constitution bars him from seeking a third term.
There was no plausible scenario in which Trump would have emerged from the midterms in a stronger position.
But the absolute thrashing Republicans took Tuesday night—far outpacing all but the most optimistic scenarios for Democrats—has accelerated Trump’s loss of power.
Eyes on 2028
In an essay-length X post yesterday, Vice President JD Vance—a likely 2028 White House contender—took care to avoid confrontation with his boss.
“The reason we lost is the war,” Vance wrote, immediately adding: “The president himself said so last night.”
That is not entirely true. Trump only partially blamed the Middle East conflict for the defeat. He also said Republicans fielded poor candidates.
Florida Governor Ron DeSantis described an “extinction-level event” for Republicans and thinks they may have to wait until 2032 to regain control of Congress.
The party “needs to reclaim our Reagan principles,” Republican lawmaker Don Bacon wrote on X. “Voters rejected populism, chaos, Putin and tariffs.”

Former congresswoman Marjorie Taylor Greene, a far-right figure who now fiercely and publicly opposes the president, said, “If the GOP wants any chance in the future, it will have to kick Donald Trump out of the party.”
“Republicans need to get back to basics,” Matthew Boyle, a leading figure at far-right news site Breitbart, wrote on X.
“No more endless wars... When it comes to the economy, the number one issue, pursue policies that help ordinary people not special interests,” he added. “And be sane with immigration enforcement.”
Criticism, not by name
But for now, the criticism remains relatively muted. Few conservative figures, whether moderate or radical, have attacked Trump by name.
The Republican Party has, after all, tied its fate entirely to the billionaire since 2016.

“The big question is, are some of these Republican leaders in the House and Senate going to distance themselves from Trump?” Amy Dacey, a former Democratic official who is now an expert at American University, told AFP.
The same goes for far-right influencers, whose audiences—and incomes—have tracked Trump’s popularity.
A stunning loss dings influence, “but this is not going to, in any way, eradicate some people who are affiliated with some of the MAGA movement,” Dacey added.
Some of MAGA’s digital foot soldiers have tried to redirect the reckoning.
“Great work, neocons,” Jack Posobiec wrote sarcastically on X, referring to a Republican faction known for interventionist foreign policy and a hawkish stance against Iran.
But it may only be a matter of time before the break becomes definitive.
Former congressman Bob Good said on the same platform: “Gotta start by acknowledging that Trump was and is the problem. Quietly whispering it won’t do it.” — AFP
eefbdc191eb82781: SEOUL, Nov 5 — North Korea test-fired a newly designed air-defence missile system and held a strategic cruise-missile strike drill, state media reported today in the latest showcase of its weapons abilities.

Wednesday’s test came during a flurry of weapons demonstrations in recent weeks that include cluster munitions, attack drones, a precision-guided torpedo system and an intermediate-range hypersonic missile.
South Korea’s military said yesterday it detected several missiles launched from the North Korea’s Sondok area into the Sea of Japan.

Pyongyang has also hardened its stance towards Seoul and Washington, with a landmine dispute plummetting inter-Korean relations and Kim Jong Un’s powerful sister this week signalling little appetite for renewed talks with the United States.
The newly designed system was test-fired to confirm its technical specifcations, the official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said today.
“The test-fire proved the technical specifications and reliability of the new material and intelligent multiple guided mode of the projectile,” KCNA said, without elaborating on the new material.
It also demonstrated the missile system’s ability to identify and track targets, as well as the reliability of its detection data processing device, it added.
KCNA also said a firepower sub-unit of a long-range strategic cruise-missile unit in eastern North Korea also staged a strike drill on Wednesday.
The unit “perfectly performed its mission to strike a virtual airport target with a long-range strategic cruise missile”, state media said.
The two exercises were aimed and maintaining weapons systems “on a technically high level and improve the combat reliability of the strategic weapon”, KCNA added.
Unlike ballistic missile launches, North Korean cruise missile tests are not prohibited by UN Security Council sanctions.
North Korea has a history of launching missiles around US elections, widely seen as a show of force, including during the midterms four years ago and the presidential election two years ago. — AFP
53527c9ce5762d95: LOS ANGELES, Nov 5 — A proposal to levy a one-off tax on billionaires in California appeared to be headed for defeat Wednesday in a vote being watched around the world at a time of growing anger over wealth disparity.
So-called Proposition 40 would force around 200 billionaires in the state to cough up five percent of their their total net worth, with the money largely dedicated to helping pay for healthcare.
But with about 60 percent of votes counted, “No” was leading by 55.6 per cent to 44.4 per cent, data showed.
An analysis by the San Francisco Chronicle looking at how the outstanding votes were expected to fall determined the result was unlikely to change.

Prop 40 was one of a bevy of proposals put to voters in Tuesday’s midterm elections, which delivered large-scale victories across the nation for the Democratic Party, and handed a drubbing to President Donald Trump’s Republicans.
With the highest population of any US state, California is notoriously slow at counting votes but a number of propositions and many elected positions—including governor—have already been decided.

The proposal was unveiled to fanfare in California, a state that would be the world’s fourth largest economy if it were a country, but one in which there is a yawning gulf between the haves and the have-nots.
It was seen by wealth tax proponents as a key part of a global effort to tackle growing income inequality.
“Significant changes rarely move in a straight line,” Nobel Prize-winning economist Joseph E. Stiglitz said in a statement sent to AFP by the International Capital Tax Commission.
“Prop 40 put a tax on billionaire wealth on the ballot in the United States for the first time,” he added.
Advocates calculated the one-off tax would raise about US$100 billion which would be used to fund a public healthcare system that has been hit by Trump’s budget cuts.
Opponents of the ballot measure, including Google co-founder Sergey Brin, raised hundreds of millions of dollars to defeat the idea, arguing it would push the wealthy to leave California.
“No” campaign commercials warning about the loss of future tax revenues if billionaires desert the state played wall-to-wall across TV stations in California in the run-up to the vote.
Outgoing Governor Gavin Newsom, who is widely expected to make a run for the White House in 2028, said he would vote no.

United Domestic Workers, a union representing 250,000 home care and childcare providers, also urged its members to vote against, arguing that the one-time tax was no way to plug multi-billion dollar holes in the state’s budget.
California has previously voted three times this decade on a wealth tax, rejecting it every time.

While the measure was popular when it was first launched, it lost steam quickly once the “No” campaign kicked into high gear, warning voters it would result in raids on their own more modest savings. — AFP

613e56f2e2a3da12: WASHINGTON: US House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries formally sought support Wednesday for his candidacy to become the next Speaker of the House of Representatives following Democratic victories in the midterm elections, Anadolu Ajansi reported.

In a letter to incoming members of the 120th Congress, Jeffries celebrated the party's electoral success, declaring that “America is back” and called for a new political direction focused on affordability, accountability and American values.
"I write to humbly request your support in connection with my candidacy to serve as the next Speaker of the House of Representatives," he said.

Jeffries pledged to prioritise lowering living costs, reversing Medicaid cuts, restoring food assistance funding, extending Affordable Care Act tax credits and eliminating Trump-era tariffs. He also called for an end to the war in Iran, which he blamed for rising gasoline prices.

Arguing that Democrats had successfully challenged the Trump administration even while in the minority, Jeffries said the party must now deliver broader policy changes with control of Congress.

d6cb83bf11021452: ALOR GAJAH: Five years after being dropped as PKR’s candidate for Machap Jaya, Ginie Lim is back in the running, describing her return as a political “comeback” after a turbulent spell marked by factional infighting, pressure to leave the party and disciplinary action.
Lim said that she had stayed loyal to PKR despite being caught up in its internal factional disputes, insisting that her allegiance was to the party and its principles, not individual leaders.
“I stayed on, even though there was a lot of pressure to push me out. I also received many invitations to join other parties, but that was never an issue for me.
“For me, politics is about testing our loyalty. It tests our persistence and commitment to the cause and the principles we uphold,” she told FMT.
Lim also said that her relationship with party leaders has improved, pointing to her appointment as Wanita PKR information chief.
She acknowledged having been suspended and facing complaints, but described those experiences as part and parcel of politics.
“I have been penalised, but I make a comeback. I make things better. I improve myself and contribute better to the party,” she said.

Her strained relationship with the PKR leadership dates back to 2019, when she and fellow assemblyman Muhamad Jailani Khamis absented themselves from a vote to nominate then Melaka PKR chief Halim Bachik as a senator.
The motion was defeated 13-12, prompting PKR president Anwar Ibrahim to condemn their absence as unacceptable.
After the 2020 Sheraton Move brought down the Pakatan Harapan federal government, PKR took action against leaders linked to Azmin Ali, who later joined Bersatu.
Lim was one of three leaders issued written warnings by the party, despite denying being aligned to him.
She was subsequently dropped as the Machap Jaya candidate ahead of the 2021 state election, a seat she won in 2018, after failing both in 2008 and 2013.
In her absence, Ngwe Hee Sem recaptured the seat for Barisan Nasional in the 2021 polls.
Lim was also suspended from duties as Alor Gajah PKR division chief in 2024 for a year, due to an alleged violation of the party’s constitution.
Although she has not held elected office for the past five years, Lim said her connection with voters in Machap Jaya had remained intact.
She said she had been inundated with “overwhelmingly encouraging messages” since being named as a candidate.

“I have maintained my connections with the community through various platforms, whether through NGOs or the service centre of Alor Gajah MP Adly Zahari. We have continued serving the community over the past five years,” she said.
“I think this explains why people still remember the warmth and friendliness we shared when I was their assemblywoman.”
Lim is in a three-corner fight for Machap Jaya, going up against incumbent Ngwe and newcomer Bersama’s B Prasanth Kumar.
fbd20b038e6787c1: PETALING JAYA: For years, an important decision often began with a Google search. But among Malaysians already comfortable with artificial intelligence, the first question is increasingly being put to an AI assistant instead.

A September survey of 1,300 adult AI users in Malaysia found that 43% turned first to AI when researching an important decision, compared with 31% who began with a search engine. The study, conducted by AI consultancy Entermind, also found that 41% had already made a purchase or financial decision primarily on information or recommendations provided by AI.
The influence appears to grow with familiarity. Among daily AI users, 52% said they had acted on AI advice, compared with 26% of those who used the technology weekly or less.

For some consumers, that marks a shift from using AI simply to draft an email, summarise a document or answer a casual question. It is increasingly becoming part of the process of choosing what to buy, where to travel or how to approach a financial decision.

The survey also found that AI's usefulness varied according to what people were trying to decide. Respondents found it particularly helpful for understanding healthcare options, comparing retail choices and discovering travel possibilities.

Yet users do not appear eager to surrender the decision altogether: 51% said they preferred a future in which AI helped guide them while they remained in control, while only 6% wanted the technology to handle most tasks on their behalf.
Its appeal may lie in reducing complexity - narrowing a long list of options, explaining unfamiliar terminology, or comparing several choices at once.

But AI-generated answers can still be incomplete or inaccurate despite sounding authoritative, making independent verification especially important for decisions involving health, money or other high-stakes matters.

Regular exposure to conversational AI further appears to be reshaping what consumers expect from conventional websites and apps. Some 78% of respondents said they wished company platforms made finding information and reaching decisions as easy as AI tools do.

That preference was reflected in how respondents wanted to navigate online services: 42% favoured a search box, compared with only 17% who preferred menus. Typing a direct question can feel considerably more intuitive than clicking through several layers of a website in search of an answer.
Entermind argues that this creates a growing gap between the relatively fluid experience people have with AI assistants and the more cumbersome experience offered by many companies' digital channels.
Consumers, it suggests, are becoming less patient with websites that make straightforward information difficult to find.

The consultancy estimates that roughly 10 million Malaysian adults in its more advanced AI-user categories account for around RM190 billion in annual household spending. Restaurants and accommodation, food and beverages, and transport are among the largest spending categories after housing and utilities.

This does not mean AI is responsible for RM190 billion in purchases. The estimate combines the proportion of adults Entermind classifies as "highly AI-savvy" with household expenditure patterns from the Malaysian statistics department.

The study is also based specifically on people who already use AI rather than Malaysians as a whole, so its findings should not be read as evidence that nearly half the country has abandoned search engines for ChatGPT and its rivals.

What it does capture is a change in behaviour among people who have embraced the technology: AI is no longer necessarily where they turn after finding information elsewhere; increasingly, it is becoming where the search itself begins.
5c01468cfa964daf: ALOR GAJAH: Lima tahun selepas digugurkan sebagai calon PKR di Machap Jaya, Ginie Lim kembali bertanding di kerusi itu dan menyifatkan pencalonannya sebagai kebangkitan semula dalam kerjaya politiknya selepas melalui pelbagai kemelut dalaman parti, tekanan supaya meninggalkan PKR serta tindakan disiplin.

Lim berkata beliau tetap setia kepada PKR walaupun pernah terpalit dalam perbalahan antara kem dalam parti, sambil menegaskan kesetiaannya kepada perjuangan dan prinsip parti, bukannya pemimpin tertentu.
"Saya tetap bertahan walaupun menerima banyak tekanan supaya keluar parti. Saya juga menerima banyak pelawaan untuk menyertai parti lain, tetapi perkara itu tidak pernah menjadi pertimbangan saya.
"Bagi saya, politik menguji kesetiaan, ketabahan dan komitmen kita terhadap perjuangan serta prinsip yang kita pegang," katanya kepada FMT.
Lim berkata hubungannya dengan kepimpinan PKR kini semakin baik, seperti dibuktikan menerusi pelantikannya sebagai ketua penerangan Wanita PKR.
Beliau mengakui pernah digantung tugas dan berdepan aduan terhadapnya, namun menganggap pengalaman itu sebagai sebahagian daripada asam garam politik.
"Saya pernah dikenakan tindakan, tetapi saya bangkit semula. Saya berusaha memperbaiki keadaan, memperbaiki diri dan memberikan sumbangan lebih baik kepada parti," katanya.

Hubungan Lim dengan kepimpinan PKR mula tegang pada 2019 apabila beliau dan seorang lagi Adun Muhamad Jailani Khamis, tidak hadir ketika pengundian usul mencalonkan ketua PKR Melaka ketika itu, Halim Bachik, sebagai senator.

Usul berkenaan gagal diluluskan apabila hanya mendapat 12 undi menyokong berbanding 13 undi menentang, menyebabkan Presiden PKR Anwar Ibrahim mengecam ketidakhadiran mereka sebagai sesuatu yang tidak boleh diterima.

Susulan Langkah Sheraton pada 2020 yang menyebabkan kerajaan persekutuan Pakatan Harapan (PH) tumbang, PKR mengambil tindakan terhadap beberapa pemimpin yang dikaitkan dengan Azmin Ali, yang kemudiannya menyertai Bersatu.
Lim adalah antara tiga pemimpin yang menerima surat amaran daripada parti walaupun beliau menafikan mempunyai kaitan dengan kem Azmin.

Beliau kemudian tidak dicalonkan untuk mempertahankan kerusi Machap Jaya pada PRN 2021, selepas memenangi kerusi itu pada 2018. Sebelum kemenangan berkenaan, Lim pernah gagal dalam percubaannya pada pilihan raya 2008 dan 2013.
Tanpa Lim sebagai calon, Barisan Nasional (BN) berjaya merampas semula kerusi Machap Jaya menerusi Ngwe Hee Sem pada PRN 2021.
Pada 2024, Lim sekali lagi berdepan tindakan disiplin apabila digantung daripada menjalankan tugas sebagai ketua PKR Cabang Alor Gajah selama setahun, susulan dakwaan melanggar perlembagaan parti.
Walaupun tidak memegang sebarang jawatan wakil rakyat sejak lima tahun lalu, Lim berkata hubungannya dengan pengundi Machap Jaya tidak pernah terputus.
Menurutnya, beliau menerima begitu banyak mesej sokongan dan kata-kata semangat sejak diumumkan sebagai calon.

"Saya terus mengekalkan hubungan dengan masyarakat melalui pelbagai saluran, sama ada menerusi NGO atau pusat khidmat Ahli Parlimen Alor Gajah, Adly Zahari. Kami tidak pernah berhenti berkhidmat kepada masyarakat sepanjang lima tahun lalu," katanya.
"Saya rasa sebab itulah penduduk masih mengingati hubungan mesra dan keakraban yang terjalin ketika saya menjadi Adun mereka."
Lim bakal berdepan pertandingan tiga penjuru di Machap Jaya menentang Ngwe, serta B Prasanth Kumar daripada Bersama.
f2cedf4b022f5e21: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar and major currencies on Thursday ahead of Bank Negara Malaysia’s (BNM) Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) decision, with expectations of an interest rate hike lending support to the local currency.
BNM’s Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) is scheduled to hold its sixth and final policy meeting of 2026 today.
At 8am, the ringgit strengthened to 4.0585/4.0660 against the US dollar from Wednesday’s close of 4.0610/4.0660.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Afzanizam Rashid said BNM is expected to raise the OPR by 25 basis points at its final MPC meeting of the year.
“We are anticipating a 25-basis-point increase could be delivered as a means to normalise its monetary policy stance after economic growth continues to exceed target this year,” he added.
On the external front, Afzanizam said improved risk appetite following the United States (US) midterm elections had also contributed to the ringgit’s positive performance.

He said the improved sentiment was reflected in global financial markets, with Brent crude oil prices falling 8.62% to US$94.67 per barrel and the yield on the 10-year US Treasury note declining eight basis points to 4.89%.
Meanwhile, the S&P 500 rose 1.58% to close at 7,688.62 points, while the US Dollar Index (DXY) fell 0.33% to 101.528 points.
Against this backdrop, Afzanizam expects the ringgit to extend its gains, with the ringgit-US dollar pair potentially testing the RM4.05 level.

Against major currencies, the ringgit edged up against the Japanese yen to 2.5628/2.5677 from 2.5636/2.5669 at Wednesday’s close. It also strengthened against the euro to 4.5601/4.5686 from 4.5723/4.5779 and the British pound to 5.4696/5.4797 from 5.4783/5.4850.
However, the ringgit traded mixed against its Asean peers.
It strengthened against the Singapore dollar to 3.1734/3.1798 from 3.1771/3.1813 at Wednesday’s close and inched up against the Indonesian rupiah to 223.4/223.8 from 223.5/223.8.
Conversely, the local note eased against the Thai baht to 12.0746/12.1037 from 12.0673/12.0868, while it was unchanged against the Philippine peso at 6.39/6.40.

e0d53d13f4be69d0: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump backed defence secretary Pete Hegseth on Wednesday, a day after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in midterm elections that reflected voter anger over the Iran war.
Asked whether he was considering replacing Hegseth, whom he has described as a champion of the war, Trump told reporters: "No, I think he's doing a very good job."

The response contrasted with then-President George Bush, who fired defence secretary Donald Rumsfeld the morning after the 2006 midterm elections, when voter discontent over the Iraq war helped Democrats win control of Congress.
But sources said Trump could still replace Hegseth as Republicans assess their losses.
One Trump adviser said Hegseth "could be on the chopping block" because of the war. "Someone is going to get blamed for this and you know it's not going to be him (Trump)," the adviser said.

Trump has described Hegseth as a key proponent of the unpopular conflict, saying on March 23: "Pete, I think you were the first one to speak up, and you said, 'Let's do it, because you can't let them have a nuclear weapon.'"
On Wednesday, vice-president JD Vance publicly questioned whether the Iran war was worth it and said it cost Republicans control of Congress.
Asked for comment, the White House referred Reuters to Trump's public remarks on Hegseth.
The defence department said Hegseth was "100% committed" to leading the Pentagon until the end of Trump's term, which ends on Jan 20, 2029.
Impeachment threat

Hegseth has been a polarising figure in American politics and has made enemies even with his own Republican Party. One Republican lawmaker, US Representative Thomas Massie, even filed articles of impeachment against him earlier this year, accusing him of abusing his ​office by launching hostilities against Iran without approval by Congress.

Republican US Senator Thom Tillis told CBS news on Tuesday night that Hegseth has "a reckoning" coming and his strained relationship with lawmakers was undermining the Trump administration's push for a US$1.5 trillion defense spending package in Congress.

"I think after the election, we need to determine whether or not he's the best person to bring those needs to Congress if he wants something done before the end of this Congress, which is only 60 days away," Tillis said as the midterm results came in.

Democrats have promised to investigate Hegseth and his handling of the Pentagon, and aides say that could include everything from his handling of the Iran war to his purges of top military officers including the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff.
He could also face scrutiny over his Ukraine policy and US military strikes on suspected drug trafficking boats in Latin American waters, which some Democrats say could amount to war crimes.

At times, the conflict between Hegseth and members of Congress has become personal. Last year, Hegseth sought to prosecute Democratic US Senator Mark Kelly after he and five other Democrats in Congress with backgrounds in the military and intelligence urged US troops to refuse illegal orders.
Hegseth accused them of sedition.

Representative Adam Smith, the Democrat who is expected to lead the House Armed Services Committee next year, promised vigorous oversight on everything from the Iran war to what he called the erosion of the "apolitical foundation of the armed forces".

A source familiar with the matter said rancor on Capitol Hill over Hegseth has featured in White House discussions about potential replacements for him, saying there would be a need to have someone in the job who could distance themselves from events under Democratic scrutiny.
Chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said Hegseth would continue to drive Trump's agenda and that the Pentagon "has followed the law."
"Secretary Hegseth will not back down or be deterred by politicians seeking to score partisan points or launch phony investigations where no wrongdoing exists," Parnell said.
Tennessee Senate seat?

One long-rumored possibility for Hegseth would be filling the Senate seat that will be vacated by Senator Marsha Blackburn, who was elected on Tuesday to become Tennessee's next governor starting in January.
She has four years left in her term, and Hegseth, a Tennessee resident who voted there on Tuesday, could be appointed to the position, without having to run for election.
Asked whether he wanted Hegseth to fill Blackburn's seat, Trump said: "Well, I think, I think he's doing a very good job, and I actually think he'd be very popular if he did that."
"But I haven't heard that at all," Trump told reporters.
Trump has regularly praised Hegseth publicly, and has given the former Army National Guard soldier significant leeway as he sought to reshape the Pentagon.
But last month Trump publicly split with Hegseth by pulling the plug on his plans to livestream the Army's firing-squad execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan.

Many fellow Republicans, along with religious leaders and international observers, raised objections to the plan. Defense officials privately expressed relief that the livestreaming would not go forward.
767b2e1af57bfeb7: HONG KONG: Activist Joshua Wong, who became the global face of Hong Kong's pro-democracy movement, is due to be sentenced on Thursday on a charge of collusion with foreign entities, which could put him behind bars for life under the city's national security law.

Now 30 years old, Wong was among a group of young people whose protest efforts have now effectively been outlawed by sweeping security legislation that Beijing imposed on the Asian financial hub in 2020.
High Court Judge William Tam is set to hand down the sentence for Wong’s conviction for foreign collusion at 9.30am Malaysian time, according to a court diary.

Wong is accused of conspiring with exiled activist Nathan Law and others to ask foreign countries, institutions, organisations or individuals outside China to impose sanctions or blockades -- or engage in other hostile activities -- against Hong Kong or China. The alleged conspiracy took place between July 1 and Nov 23, 2020.

Wong is already in jail serving a sentence on an earlier national security charge of conspiracy to commit subversion after he was among a group of pro-democratic activists who participated in an unofficial primary election in 2020.
That sentence was due to end in 2027.
The 2020 primary was an unofficial vote aimed at picking the pro-democracy camp's strongest candidates and helping it secure a majority in Hong Kong's legislature.

Prosecutors accused the activists of plotting to use control of the legislature to block government budgets and ultimately force the city's leader to resign, a strategy that authorities said amounted to subversion.
